argument.text: For any mean-zero L^2 f, Cauchy-Schwarz in its Fourier series gives ||Dinv f||_infinity<=(sum_(k!=0)k^(-2))^(1/2)||f||_2, and coefficient weights give ||Dinv f||_(H^1)<=sqrt(2)||f||_2. For a general H^1 function its mean plus this estimate for its derivative gives ||A0||_infinity<=C||A0||_(H^1). The product rule then gives ||A0*B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1). Apply it to S_t Dinv f and S_t Dinv g and use S_t isometric and P contractive to obtain ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. Each assertion is quantified over inputs in its indicated space.

produces.statement: The inverse derivative, H^1 algebra and J_t:H^0 times H^0 -> H^1 bounds stated in N005 hold uniformly in t.

argument.text: For L^2 f,g, every Fourier coefficient of the product (S_t f)(S_t g) has modulus <=||f||_2||g||_2 by Cauchy-Schwarz in the convolution. Hence ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))^2<=||f||_2^2||g||_2^2 sum_(k!=0) k^2<k>^(-2*pstar), a finite sum because pstar=23/14>3/2. The same coefficient bound with sum k^(-2) proves ||Dinv P(f*g)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A0, <k>^(-pstar)<=|k|^(-1), so ||A0||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A0||_2. Finally J_t(A0,g) is a product of S_t Dinv A0 in L^2 and S_t Dinv g in L^infinity, followed by contractions, so its L^2 norm is <=C||Dinv A0||_2||g||_2 by F001. Approximation by polynomials and these continuous bilinear bounds justify the products and their extensions.

produces.statement: The B_t negative-norm estimate, the inverse-product estimate and both asymmetric negative-norm/J estimates of N005 hold.

argument.text: For the normal-form clause take smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b]. At k!=0 the coefficient of J_t is sum_(r+s=k) exp(-i*t*3*k*r*s)*(i*r)^(-1)*(i*s)^(-1)*hat f(r)*hat g(s). Differentiating the phase gives 3*i*k times the product coefficients. Therefore d_t J_t(f,g)=3*B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Smooth spatial Fourier series and all derivatives used here converge absolutely, so differentiation and integration are legitimate. Integration gives the displayed two-endpoint normal form. For piecewise smooth continuous paths apply this on each subinterval; intermediate J endpoint values cancel because the paths are continuous.

produces.statement: The two-endpoint normal-form identity in N005 holds for smooth and continuous piecewise smooth mean-zero paths.

argument.text: Symmetry of J is immediate from the product formula. Since Dinv partial_x=P, substitution gives J_t(B_t(f,g),h)=S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f)(S_t g)]*(S_t Dinv h)}, whose integral on I is exactly Ctri_I(f,g,h); no inverse derivative is commuted through a product. For constant f,g, integrate F003 and multiply by 1/2 to obtain Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/6)[J_s(f,g)]_a^t. This establishes every identity asserted in N005.

locals.declaration: Use a_gamma=1/2-gamma for gamma<1/2, 1/8 for gamma=1/2, and 0 for gamma>1/2.

argument.text: Apply E003 on I=[a,b]. For the time-dependent assertion take its alpha=0: each smooth spatial path is in L^infinity L^2 and its piecewise derivative is in H^(-pstar); time continuity removes jump masses. The source allows each choice of negative-norm slot. For the time-independent assertion use arbitrary 0<=sigma<=1 as its alpha and constant H^sigma inputs, whose derivatives are zero. Put c0=sqrt(2*pi). Every source spatial norm and every source X norm is c0 times ours, so dividing its inequalities by c0 changes their constants by c0^2 and leaves all time powers and uniformities unchanged. This proves both normalized Ctri bounds, first for the stated paths and then by their bounded extensions.

produces.statement: Both normalized Ctri inequalities in N006 hold, with the stated slot and exponent ranges and uniform constants.

argument.text: H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. Define a_gamma as stated. E005 with source sigma=gamma, choosing endpoint epsilon=1/8 when gamma=1/2, gives the product estimate; division by c0 changes its constant by c0. The three cases give a_gamma in [0,1). The gamma=0 product case of E005 is not needed.

produces.statement: a_gamma is in [0,1) and ||f*g||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^(a_gamma)) for all such f,g.

argument.text: Fix a,tau,t,w,M0 and assume L1: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. Set wshift=S_a w. It is mean-zero and has the same H^gamma norm. From the definitions B_(a+r)(f,g)=S_(-a)B_r(S_a f,S_a g), hence Fstage_(a,t)(w)=S_(-a)Fstage_(0,t-a)(wshift). Apply E004 with source n=0, timestep tau, s=t-a, sigma=gamma, f=g=wshift and beta=a_gamma; take epsilon=1/8 in the middle case. All are in its interval: beta0<=a_gamma<=1+gamma in each of the three cases. The exponents are (1/2+2*gamma)/(5/2-gamma) for gamma<1/2, 11/17 for gamma=1/2, and (1+gamma)/2 for gamma>1/2. They are at least gamma: in the first case the numerator minus gamma times its denominator is 1/2-gamma/2+gamma^2>0; in the second 11/17>1/2; in the third 1>=gamma. Since tau<=1 these source powers are <=tau^gamma. Divide by c0 and use the S isometry to obtain the first stage bound.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_(a<=t<=a+tau)||Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau^gamma.

argument.text: Apply E004 again to the same wshift and time parameters with beta=1+gamma, which is the upper permitted endpoint. Its exponent is zero, giving ||Fstage_(0,t-a)(wshift)||_(H^(1+gamma))<=C_gamma||wshift||_(H^gamma)^2 after the same norm conversion. Use the S isometry to obtain the uniform second bound. Discharge L1 and quantify the inputs and interval. With F001-F003 this proves N006.

hypothesis_checks: The local endpoints satisfy 0<=a<=b<=a+1; sigma is universally in [0,1], while alpha=0 is allowed in part (1).
The paths have the declared continuous piecewise smooth regularity and weak derivative in H^(-pstar); constant H^sigma inputs have derivative zero.
The inputs of the second assertion are explicitly time-independent.

hypothesis_checks: H002 supplies 0<gamma<=1 and 1/8 is positive in the stated endpoint convention.
The product assertion fixes precisely f in H^gamma and g in H^(a_gamma); it introduces no stronger input condition.

tau>0, n=0 is a nonnegative integer and t-a is in [0,tau].
The displayed case calculation shows beta0<=a_gamma<=1+gamma; epsilon=1/8 is the fixed positive middle-case value.

argument.text: Fix tau>0. N005 makes Dinv:L^2->H^1 bounded and H^1 an algebra. Therefore Ftau is a continuous quadratic map L^2->H^1. In Htau the first product has factors S_tau Dinv f and Dinv Ftau(f) in H^1; the second uses the continuous bilinear mean P0(f^2) and S_tau Dinv f; the third is an H^1 cube followed by Dinv and S; the fourth multiplies S_(s-tau)Dinv2 Ftau(f) by S_s Dinv f in H^1, followed by Dinv2 and S, evaluated at two endpoints. Every coefficient, including 1/tau, is finite at this fixed tau. Hence all four terms, Ftau and Psi_tau are continuous in L^2. Fourier conjugate symmetry is preserved by S, Dinv, products and real coefficients. Every projected or inverse-derivative term has zero mean, and the unprojected second term of Htau is a scalar times the mean-zero S_tau Dinv f. Thus the update is real and mean-zero. The same formulas preserve spatial smoothness. Finite induction gives the asserted well-defined finite trajectories and continuous dependence at fixed tau.

produces.statement: For each fixed tau>0 the full update Psi_tau is continuous on real mean-zero L^2, preserves that subspace and smoothness, and Ftau maps continuously to H^1.

argument.text: For the endpoint identity now take smooth real mean-zero f and integer n>=0. Apply E006 with precisely this f,n,tau. Its exponential convention agrees with S_(-t), and its F^n and A^n are respectively Fstage and the displayed B integral; its R_2^n is D015 with t0=n*tau. This gives exactly the asserted twisted update. There is no norm conversion in this algebraic identity.

produces.statement: The exact twisted update displayed in N007 holds for every smooth real mean-zero f,n,tau.

argument.text: At t=t_n, all stage integrals in Interp vanish and its affine correction is zero, so Vst(t_n)=f. At t=t_n+tau, Q(t) cancels its contribution to W and Vst=f+Fstage+Cst-Rem. With f=v^n, F002 identifies this as v^(n+1). F001 ensures the next state remains smooth and real mean-zero. Thus adjacent pieces have matching endpoints, and the concatenation is continuous and piecewise smooth, real and mean-zero. This proves N007.

applications.bindings: Source n=n, timestep=tau, twisted datum=f; physical input=S_(n*tau)f, output=Psi_tau(S_(n*tau)f).
hypothesis_checks: The local tau is positive and n is a nonnegative integer.
The identity clause explicitly fixes f smooth, real and mean-zero; D009-D011 retain every term of source (1.4), including 1/(27*tau).

locals.declaration: Let F be the corresponding component of Interp_(a,tau;f).
Let z be the corresponding component of Interp_(a,tau;f).
Let Cst be the corresponding component of Interp_(a,tau;f).
Let Q be the corresponding component of Interp_(a,tau;f).
Let W be the corresponding component of Interp_(a,tau;f).
Let Vst be the corresponding component of Interp_(a,tau;f).
Let Y be the corresponding component of Interp_(a,tau;f).
Use the piecewise exponent specified in N006.

argument.text: Fix the local a,tau,M0,f,w, and assume L1: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and delta=||f-w||_2<=1. H002 gives 0<gamma<=1, hence q=tau^gamma+delta<=2 and ||f||_2<=M0+1. Take the tuple from Interp and the exponent a_gamma from N006. By the endpoint formula in N005, F(t)=(1/6)[J_s(f,f)]_a^t. The J:H^0 times H^0->H^1 bound gives sup||F||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0). Expanding J(f,f)-J(w,w) as J(f-w,f)+J(w,f-w) gives sup||F-Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta. Since a_gamma<1, N006 now yields sup(||F||_(H^(a_gamma))+||F||_2)<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Also z=f+F has bounded L^2 norm and z'=F'=(1/2)B_t(f,f), whose H^(-pstar) norm is bounded by N005, so ||z||_X<=C_(gamma,M0).

produces.statement: Under L1, ||f||_2<=M0+1, q<=2, the H^1 stage and stage-difference bounds in N008 hold, sup(||F||_(H^(a_gamma))+||F||_2)<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, and ||z||_X<=C_(gamma,M0).

argument.text: Set Astage=Fstage_(a,t)(w) and Dstage=F-Astage. Apply the product bound in N006 to partial_x(S_t Astage) and S_t Astage, using the H^(1+gamma) and H^(a_gamma) stage bounds. It gives ||partial_x[(S_t Astage)^2]||_2<=2*C_gamma||Astage||_(H^(1+gamma))||Astage||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau^gamma. The difference of squares is (S_t Dstage)*S_t(F+Astage). The H^1 algebra estimate in N005 and F001 give its derivative norm <=C_(gamma,M0)*delta. Therefore sup_I||B_t(F,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Integrating yields sup||Q||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q. N004 with exponent gamma and the current f,w then bounds Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f) by the same quantity, so ||W||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_I||B_t(F,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q and sup_I||Q||_2+||W||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

argument.text: Since Dinv B_t(f,F)=S_(-t)P[(S_t f)(S_t F)], split f=w+(f-w). N006 bounds the w product by C_gamma||w||_(H^gamma)||F||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q using F001. For the other product use ||f-w||_2||S_t F||_infinity<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta by the uniform H^1 stage bound and N005. Thus sup||Dinv B_t(f,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Differentiating the definition Y=Cst+Q-((t-a)/tau)W gives Y'=B_t(f,F)+(1/2)B_t(F,F)-W/tau. N005, F002 and this asymmetric product estimate give sup||Dinv Y'||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. As Y(a)=0, integration gives sup||Dinv Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

produces.statement: Under L1, the Dinv B_t(f,F) bound, the exact Y' formula, sup||Dinv Y'||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q and sup||Dinv Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q all hold.

argument.text: Apply the normal form of N005 to Cst=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s))ds, with f constant, F(a)=0 and F'=(1/2)B(f,f). Symmetry and the J(B,h)-to-Ctri identity give exactly Cst(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F(t))-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](f,f,f). Its J term is O(q) in L^2 by N005 and F001. In its Ctri term use N006 with exponent gamma on (w,w,w) to get O(tau^gamma). Expand the difference from (f,f,f) into three trilinear differences and use N006 with exponent zero on each; their size is O(delta*(||f||_2+||w||_2)^2). Thus sup||Cst||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. With F002 in Y=Cst+Q-affine W this gives sup||Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

produces.statement: Under L1, Cst(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F(t))-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](f,f,f), and sup_I||Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

argument.text: All stage components are mean-zero because B and Rem have zero output mean. N005 gives ||Y'||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv Y'||_2 and ||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv Y||_2. Combine F003 and F004 to obtain ||Y||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q and sup||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q. These constants depend only on gamma and M0; none uses a higher norm of f.

produces.statement: Under L1, ||Y||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q and sup_I||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

argument.text: Collect F001-F005. Discharge L1 and universally quantify all the step data. This proves every clause of N008.

locals.declaration: Fix a step start a, later a grid starting point for I.
Fix f satisfying the conditional step hypotheses.
Fix w satisfying the conditional step hypotheses.
Use Y from the current step tuple.
Use z from the current step tuple.
Use W from the current step tuple.
Use Vst from the current step tuple.
Define rho by the three integrals/affine term in N009.
Fix an exact twisted path v.
Let V be the interpolation of the smooth numerical trajectory from N007.
Concatenate the step increments rho with initial value zero.

argument.text: First fix a step with the antecedent L1 of N008: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0, delta=||f-w||_2<=1, with smooth real mean-zero f,w, M0>=1 and the stated a,tau. Use its tuple and q. Differentiation of Interp gives Vst'=(1/2)B_t(z,z)-W/tau. Since Vst=z+Y, subtraction of (1/2)B_t(Vst,Vst) gives rho'=-B_t(Y,z)-(1/2)B_t(Y,Y)-W/tau. The residual increment vanishes at a. N008 bounds ||Y||_2 by C*q, ||z||_2 by C and ||W||_2/tau by C*q, with q<=2. N005 thus gives ||rho'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

produces.statement: Under L1 the differential residual identity holds and ||rho'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

argument.text: For the first integral in rho apply N005's normal form to (Y,z). Its boundary J terms are O(tau*q) using ||Dinv Y||_2<=C*tau*q from N008 and bounded ||z||_2. The integral containing Y' is O(tau*q) by the asymmetric J bound and ||Dinv Y'||_2<=C*q. Since z'=(1/2)B_t(f,f), symmetry turns the remaining term into a fixed multiple of Ctri_[a,t](f,f,Y). Apply N006 with the negative norm on Y: N008 gives ||Y||_X<=C*q and ||Y||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C*tau*q, while f is constant with L^2 norm <=M0+1. Hence this term too is O(tau*q), even on a partial step.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_(a<=t<=a+tau)||integral_a^t B_s(Y,z)ds||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

argument.text: For integral B(Y,Y), apply the same normal form with Y in both slots. Boundary terms use ||Dinv Y||_2||Y||_2<=C*tau*q^2, and derivative integrals use ||Dinv Y'||_2||Y||_2<=C*q^2 over length tau. Thus it is O(tau*q^2)=O(tau*q) because q<=2. The affine W term is O(tau*q) by N008. Combine with F001-F002 to prove both residual estimates on the whole or any initial part of the step. Discharge L1 and quantify the data.

produces.statement: For every step satisfying the N008 hypotheses, the exact residual identities and both quantitative step bounds in N009 hold.

argument.text: Now fix a smooth numerical trajectory and exact twisted v and assume L2: sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), I=[a,b] starts at a grid point, h<=1 and E_I=sup_I||v-V||_2<=1. N007 gives the continuous interpolation V with grid values v^n. Concatenate the residual increments, obtaining Rres and V'=(1/2)B(V,V)+Rres' stepwise and distributionally. At each intersected step start t_n, delta_n=||v^n-v(t_n)||_2=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I, so its q_n<=tau^gamma+E_I and F003 applies with w=v(t_n),f=v^n. There are at most h/tau+1 intersected steps; the last can be partial. Sum the step increment bounds to obtain sup_I||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I). Also sup||Rres'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

produces.statement: Under L2, the accumulated residual bound in N009 holds, and ||Rres'||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar)))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

argument.text: Under L2, ||v||_(L^infinity L^2)<=M0 and ||V||_(L^infinity L^2)<=M0+1. Subtract the equations to obtain e'=B_t(e,v-e/2)-Rres'. N005 and F004 imply ||e'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), so ||e||_X has the same bound. The exact equation bounds ||v'||_(H^(-pstar)), and V=v-e then has bounded X norm too, since tau^gamma+E_I<=2. This proves the remaining assertions. Discharge L2 and quantify the trajectory and interval.

locals.declaration: Fix 0<tau<=1, with the smaller final restriction imposed later.
Fix the exact twisted path v.
Fix the interpolation V of the specified numerical trajectory.
Fix a grid starting point a.
Use the concatenated step residual defined by N009.
Fix an arbitrary proof-only threshold N>=2.
Choose C0>=1 dominating the finite constants in F005, uniformly over admissible intervals and trajectories.

argument.text: Assume L1: the smooth real mean-zero v satisfies v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, and the numerical interpolation V is taken on an interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, h<=1, E_I<=1. Set e=v-V,g=v-e/2 and take the concatenated Rres from N009. Its conclusions apply to this trajectory and give the accumulated residual and X bounds. In particular e'=B_t(e,g)-Rres', so integration gives e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)). Also ||e||_X<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||v||_X+||V||_X+||g||_X<=C_(gamma,M0).

produces.statement: Under L1 the exact error identity and the residual/X bounds of N009 hold on I; g=v-e/2 has bounded X norm.

argument.text: Fix N>=2 only in the proof. For each time s, the inverse-product bound of N005 and the Fourier inequality ||Ple_N partial_x^2 A||_2<=N^2||A||_2 give ||Ple_N B_s(e,g)||_2<=C*N^2||e||_2||g||_2. Indeed B_s(e,g)=S_(-s)partial_x^2 Dinv P[(S_s e)(S_s g)]. Integrate over length at most h and use bounded ||g||_2 to obtain sup||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1, for every N>=2, sup_I||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I.

argument.text: Apply the two-endpoint normal form N005 to F_I. The equations give e'=B(e,g)-Rres' and g'=(1/2)B(v,v)-(1/2)B(e,g)+(1/2)Rres'. In the differentiated J terms, its symmetry and integral J(B,h)=Ctri give Ctri(e,g,g)-(1/2)Ctri(e,g,e)=Ctri(e,g,V), since g-e/2=V. The other cubic term is (1/2)Ctri(v,v,e), and the forcing terms satisfy -J(Rres',g)+(1/2)J(e,Rres')=-J(Rres',V). Multiplication by -1/3 yields F_I=(1/3)[J_s(e,g)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds. Both endpoints are retained. Apply the H^1 bound for J in N005: their projections above N are <=C_(gamma,M0)*N^(-1)*E_I. Continuity of all the paths makes internal endpoints cancel when the normal form is applied stepwise.

produces.statement: Under L1, the full normal-form identity in N010 holds and its two endpoint contributions above N have norm <=C_(gamma,M0)*N^(-1)*E_I.

argument.text: For any three admissible paths on I, put Lproj=Ple_(N/3),Hproj=I-Lproj. The telescoping expansion Ctri(f_1,f_2,f_3)-Ctri(Lproj f_1,Lproj f_2,Lproj f_3)=Ctri(Hproj f_1,f_2,f_3)+Ctri(Lproj f_1,Hproj f_2,f_3)+Ctri(Lproj f_1,Lproj f_2,Hproj f_3) places a high input in each term. The all-low term has no output above N because all product frequencies sum. Each projection contracts both components of X and ||Hproj f_i||_(H^(-pstar))<=C*N^(-pstar)||f_i||_2 by Fourier weights. Apply N006 with the negative norm on that particular high slot. This proves ||Pgt_N Ctri_I(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C*h*product_j||f_j||_X+C*N^(-pstar)*product_j||f_j||_(L^infinity L^2). argument.text: Let useq_m be the exact flows and unumseq_m their numerical trajectories. definitions.definition: Torus=R/(2*pi*Z), with measure dx/(2*pi) on [0,2*pi).
For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).

definitions.type: homogeneous Sobolev norms on the mean-zero subspaces

definitions.definition: S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
pstar=23/14.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.

KdV(u;u_0) means u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u_0 on Torus, distributionally. The exact solution sought for real mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation. This predicate itself asserts no existence or quantitative bound.

inputs.statement: 0<gamma<=1.

For the real mean-zero periodic equation U_t=U*U_x+U_xxx on R/(2*pi*Z), use hat U(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral U(x)exp(-i*k*x)dx, ||U||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2s)|hat U(k)|^2, and z_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t)hat U(t)(k). For every s>0 and horizon Q>0, every initial datum U_0 in dot H^s has a distributional solution with z in C([0,Q];dot H^s), unique in the source solution class (z in L^infinity dot H^0 satisfying z_k(t)-z_k(0)=(i*k/2)integral_0^t sum_(k1+k2=k)exp(i*3*k*k1*k2*r)z_k1(r)z_k2(r)dr). Its dot H^0 norm is conserved, and the flow depends Lipschitz continuously on the initial data in dot H^s, uniformly on bounded dot H^s sets on [0,Q]. The Galerkin approximations (with the nonlinear inputs and output projected to |k|<=m and high coefficients frozen) have dot H^s bounds uniform in m, depending only on s,Q, the initial dot H^s norm and an upper bound for the initial dot H^0 norm. For 0<sigma<s they admit a subsequence converging strongly in L^q([0,Q];dot H^sigma), 1<q<infinity, and weak-* in L^infinity dot H^s to this solution; the same dot H^s bound holds for the limit. For s=0 there is a unique C([0,Q];dot H^0) solution, conserving that norm and depending Lipschitz continuously on its data. These flows agree on overlapping regularity classes and are obtained by smooth approximation.
source_conditions: The torus has length 2*pi, the datum is real and mean-zero.
The horizon Q is positive and the nonnegative Sobolev regularity and initial norms are as stated.

inputs.statement: For Q>0, theta in (-1,0] and real mean-zero initial data U_0,W_0 in dot H^0 with ||U_0||_(dot H^0)+||W_0||_(dot H^0)<=B0, the two source twisted solutions z,y of z_k'=(i*k/2)sum_(k1+k2=k) exp(i*3*k*k1*k2*t)z_k1*z_k2 with these initial coefficients satisfy sup_(0<=t<=Q)||z(t)-y(t)||_(dot H^theta)<=C'(B0,theta)*C_(B0,theta)^Q*||U_0-W_0||_(dot H^theta). The constants depend only on B0,theta. Since the untwisting multiplier is common and unitary, the same estimate holds for the physical source fields U,W.
source_conditions: Q>0 and -1<theta<=0.
The two data are real, mean-zero L^2 data and their dot H^0 norms sum to at most B0.

output.statement: There is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero datum a0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||a0||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique real mean-zero exact KdV solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma), obtained by smooth approximation, satisfying sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth data have smooth solutions. If a0,b0 are two such data then sup_[0,T]||u_a0(t)-u_b0(t)||_2<=K(T,2*R)||a0-b0||_2. The same estimate holds for any two real mean-zero L^2 data with sum of norms <=2*R. Twisting v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) preserves these bounds; for smooth data v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v). Thus M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma)<=1+A uniformly on the original ball.

argument.text: Choose U from F001 and set u(t,x)=-U(t,-x). For smooth solutions u_t=-U_t, u_x=U_x and u_xxx=U_xxx at (t,-x), so u_t+u_xxx=-UU_x=u*u_x=(1/2)partial_x(u^2). The same equality follows distributionally by the reflection change of variables for the limiting solution. Fourier coefficients satisfy hat u(t)(k)=-hat U(t)(-k), hence all Sobolev norms, zero mean and reality are preserved. The comparison ||u||_(H^gamma)<=2^(gamma/2)||U||_(dot H^gamma) gives a bound A(T,gamma,R). Finite Fourier norm sums pass to the limit under smooth approximation, and their supremum gives the full bound; continuity gives it for every time. argument.text: Integration by parts against exp(-i*beta*s), which has nonzero derivative factor -i*beta under L1, gives |eta|<= (|h(0)|+|h(tau)|+integral|h'|)/(tau|beta|)<=2|alpha/beta| by F001. Take their minima, discharge L1, and include the zero-phase case already calculated. Universal introduction proves the output assertion.

argument.text: For the pointwise assertions fix integers a,b,c,d and assume L1: abcd!=0 and a+b+c+d=0. Order their magnitudes as N1>=N2>=N3>=N4. The largest is bounded by the sum of the other three, so N1<=3*N2. Put A0=|ab|, B0=|cd|. If d is among the two largest, min(A0/B0,B0/A0)<=1 and 1/|d|<=1/N3. If not, the largest two are among a,b,c. If they are a,b, use B0/A0 to bound the desired expression by |c|/|ab|<=1/N3. If they are a,c, their ratio lies in [1/3,3]. Therefore the expression is at most 3*min(|b|/|d|^2,1/|b|)<=3/max(|b|,|d|)=3/N3: use the first alternative if |d|>=|b| and the second otherwise. The case b,c is identical after swapping a,b. This proves the first majorant.

argument.text: For the second majorant, if the two largest are in the same pair of (a,b),(c,d), the other pair sums to magnitude at most 2*N3. Since a+b=-(c+d), |a+b|/max(A0,B0)<=2*N3/(N1*N2)<=2/N3. If they lie in different pairs, the third largest is paired with one of them, whence max(A0,B0)>=N2*N3; also |a+b|<=2*N1<=6*N2 by F001. The quotient is <=6/N3. Any ordering of ties is covered. Discharge L1; these are the claimed conditional pointwise statements for all such frequencies.

Fix four nonnegative ell^2 sequences x_r. First restrict all of them to finitely many frequencies. Decompose each into shells 2^j<=|k|<2^(j+1), j>=0, and let Xshell_(r,j) be its ell^2 norm there. Fix one of the at most 24 orderings of the four shell indices j1>=j2>=j3>=j4, permuting the sequence labels accordingly. A nonzero zero-sum interaction requires j1-j2<=2, since otherwise the largest magnitude would exceed the sum of the other three. For each fixed pair of the two smaller frequencies, sum the two larger-frequency sequences subject to their prescribed sum. Cauchy-Schwarz, applied to a translated reflection, bounds that sum by their shell ell^2 norm product. A shell contains at most 2^(j+1) integers, so summing each smaller sequence in ell^1 costs at most C*2^(j/2) times its ell^2 norm. Thus the shell contribution without the weight is <=C*2^((j3+j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr). On that shell N3>=2^j3, so the weight leaves C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2).

produces.statement: For every ordered four-shell zero-sum interaction j1>=j2>=j3>=j4, its weighted contribution is <=C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr), and j1-j2 is in {0,1,2}.

argument.text: For each q in {0,1,2}, set j1=J,j2=J-q. Drop the upper restrictions on the smaller shells; nonnegativity increases the sum. F002 bounds the ordered contribution by C*(sum_J Xshell_(1,J)*Xshell_(2,J-q))*(sum_(ell>=m>=0)2^(-(ell-m)/2)*Xshell_(3,ell)*Xshell_(4,m)). The first factor is at most ||Xshell_1||_ell2||Xshell_2||_ell2. Set r=ell-m; for each r the second correlation is at most ||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2 by Cauchy-Schwarz, so the second factor is at most sum_(r>=0)2^(-r/2)||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2=||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2/(1-2^(-1/2)). Shell disjointness identifies each shell-norm ell^2 norm with ||x_r||_ell2. Sum over 24 orderings and three offsets. This proves the finite bound with an absolute constant.

produces.statement: The four-linear bound in the output assertion holds for finite restrictions with an absolute constant independent of the supports.

Restricting to any subset only decreases that nonnegative sum. Together with the pointwise assertions this proves the output assertion without exchanging conditionally convergent sums.

argument.text: Fix tau>0. N005 makes Dinv:L^2->H^1 bounded and H^1 an algebra. Therefore Ftau is a continuous quadratic map L^2->H^1. In Htau the first product has factors S_tau Dinv f and Dinv Ftau(f) in H^1; the second uses the continuous bilinear mean P0(f^2) and S_tau Dinv f; the third is an H^1 cube followed by Dinv and S; the fourth multiplies S_(s-tau)Dinv2 Ftau(f) by S_s Dinv f in H^1, followed by Dinv2 and S, evaluated at two endpoints. Every coefficient, including 1/tau, is finite at this fixed tau. Hence all four terms, Ftau and Psi_tau are continuous in L^2. Fourier conjugate symmetry is preserved by S, Dinv, products and real coefficients. Every projected or inverse-derivative term has zero mean, and the unprojected second term of Htau is a scalar times the mean-zero S_tau Dinv f. Thus the update is real and mean-zero. The same formulas preserve spatial smoothness. Finite induction gives the asserted well-defined finite trajectories and continuous dependence at fixed tau.

definitions.definition: Torus=R/(2*pi*Z), with measure dx/(2*pi) on [0,2*pi).
For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).
S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
P0 f=hat f(0), the mean, identified with a constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1); hat(Dinv f)(k)=(i*k)^(-1)hat f(k) for k!=0 and zero for k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). These formulas define maps H^s -> H^(s+1) and H^s -> H^(s+2), respectively.

Take the tuple from Interp and the exponent a_gamma from N006. By the endpoint formula in N005, F(t)=(1/6)[J_s(f,f)]_a^t. The J:H^0 times H^0->H^1 bound gives sup||F||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0). Expanding J(f,f)-J(w,w) as J(f-w,f)+J(w,f-w) gives sup||F-Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta. Since a_gamma<1, N006 now yields sup(||F||_(H^(a_gamma))+||F||_2)<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Also z=f+F has bounded L^2 norm and z'=F'=(1/2)B_t(f,f), whose H^(-pstar) norm is bounded by N005, so ||z||_X<=C_(gamma,M0).

argument.text: Set Astage=Fstage_(a,t)(w) and Dstage=F-Astage. Apply the product bound in N006 to partial_x(S_t Astage) and S_t Astage, using the H^(1+gamma) and H^(a_gamma) stage bounds. It gives ||partial_x[(S_t Astage)^2]||_2<=2*C_gamma||Astage||_(H^(1+gamma))||Astage||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau^gamma. The difference of squares is (S_t Dstage)*S_t(F+Astage). The H^1 algebra estimate in N005 and F001 give its derivative norm <=C_(gamma,M0)*delta. Therefore sup_I||B_t(F,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Integrating yields sup||Q||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q. N004 with exponent gamma and the current f,w then bounds Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f) by the same quantity, so ||W||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

argument.text: Since Dinv B_t(f,F)=S_(-t)P[(S_t f)(S_t F)], split f=w+(f-w). N006 bounds the w product by C_gamma||w||_(H^gamma)||F||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q using F001. For the other product use ||f-w||_2||S_t F||_infinity<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta by the uniform H^1 stage bound and N005. Thus sup||Dinv B_t(f,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. produces.statement: Under L1, the Dinv B_t(f,F) bound, the exact Y' formula, sup||Dinv Y'||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q and sup||Dinv Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q all hold.

argument.text: Apply the normal form of N005 to Cst=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s))ds, with f constant, F(a)=0 and F'=(1/2)B(f,f). Symmetry and the J(B,h)-to-Ctri identity give exactly Cst(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F(t))-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](f,f,f). Its J term is O(q) in L^2 by N005 and F001. Expand the difference from (f,f,f) into three trilinear differences and use N006 with exponent zero on each; their size is O(delta*(||f||_2+||w||_2)^2). Thus sup||Cst||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. definitions.type: average covariance of two exponential phases
definitions.definition:
For real alpha,beta,
M_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds,
eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
The notation M_tau here means Mavg_tau; eta_tau is the family eta at timestep tau.

For tau>0,t0>=0 and mean-zero trigonometric polynomials f_1,f_2,f_3, define hat(Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3))(k)=-tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f_1(a)*hat f_2(b)*hat f_3(c) for k!=0, and zero at k=0. The extension to Sobolev inputs is a proved conclusion below, not an assumed estimate. The same Fourier formula defines the operator for smooth inputs by absolutely convergent series: |eta|<=2 from the two averages and smooth Fourier coefficients are rapidly decreasing, so the triple sum is absolutely convergent. The polynomial restriction is its initial dense core.
pstar=23/14.

inputs.statement: The following estimates have constants uniform in the real time t. For mean-zero f in L^2, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2. For f,g in L^2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(f*g)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For 0<gamma<=1 set a_gamma=1/2-gamma when gamma<1/2, a_gamma=1/8 when gamma=1/2, and a_gamma=0 when gamma>1/2. Then a_gamma in [0,1), ||f*g||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^(a_gamma)). inputs.statement: For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau is a continuous map on the real mean-zero L^2 space, preserves mean zero and reality, and maps smooth data to smooth data; Ftau:L^2->H^1 is continuous. output.statement: For 0<gamma<=1, M0>=1, a>=0,0<tau<=1 and smooth mean-zero real f,w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and ||f-w||_2<=1, put q=tau^gamma+||f-w||_2 and take the tuple (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y)=Interp_(a,tau;f); define rho(t)=-integral_a^t B_s(Y,z)ds-(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(Y,Y)ds-((t-a)/tau)*W on [a,a+tau]. Then Vst'=(1/2)B_t(Vst,Vst)+rho', rho'=-B_t(Y,z)-(1/2)B_t(Y,Y)-W/tau, sup||rho||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q, and ||rho'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. On a smooth numerical trajectory and smooth exact twisted solution v with sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, concatenate these increments into Rres(0)=0, and let V be its continuous concatenation with grid values V(t_n)=v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. Then V'=(1/2)B_t(V,V)+Rres'. If I=[a,b] starts at a grid point, h=b-a<=1, e=v-V and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, including an endpoint inside a step, one has sup_(t in I)||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_(X(I))+||V||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0). The constants are independent of grid index, timestep, spectral support and higher norms.

locals.declaration: Fix a step start a, later a grid starting point for I.
Fix f satisfying the conditional step hypotheses.
Fix w satisfying the conditional step hypotheses.
Use Y from the current step tuple.
Use z from the current step tuple.
Use W from the current step tuple.
Use Vst from the current step tuple.
Fix an exact twisted path v.
Let V be the interpolation of the smooth numerical trajectory from N007.
Concatenate the step increments rho with initial value zero.

argument.text: First fix a step with the antecedent L1 of N008: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0, delta=||f-w||_2<=1, with smooth real mean-zero f,w, M0>=1 and the stated a,tau. Use its tuple and q. Differentiation of Interp gives Vst'=(1/2)B_t(z,z)-W/tau. Since Vst=z+Y, subtraction of (1/2)B_t(Vst,Vst) gives rho'=-B_t(Y,z)-(1/2)B_t(Y,Y)-W/tau. The residual increment vanishes at a. N008 bounds ||Y||_2 by C*q, ||z||_2 by C and ||W||_2/tau by C*q, with q<=2. N005 thus gives ||rho'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

produces.statement: Under L1 the differential residual identity holds and ||rho'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

argument.text: For the first integral in rho apply N005's normal form to (Y,z). Its boundary J terms are O(tau*q) using ||Dinv Y||_2<=C*tau*q from N008 and bounded ||z||_2. The integral containing Y' is O(tau*q) by the asymmetric J bound and ||Dinv Y'||_2<=C*q. Since z'=(1/2)B_t(f,f), symmetry turns the remaining term into a fixed multiple of Ctri_[a,t](f,f,Y). Apply N006 with the negative norm on Y: N008 gives ||Y||_X<=C*q and ||Y||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C*tau*q, while f is constant with L^2 norm <=M0+1. Hence this term too is O(tau*q), even on a partial step.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_(a<=t<=a+tau)||integral_a^t B_s(Y,z)ds||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

argument.text: For integral B(Y,Y), apply the same normal form with Y in both slots. Boundary terms use ||Dinv Y||_2||Y||_2<=C*tau*q^2, and derivative integrals use ||Dinv Y'||_2||Y||_2<=C*q^2 over length tau. Thus it is O(tau*q^2)=O(tau*q) because q<=2. The affine W term is O(tau*q) by N008. Combine with F001-F002 to prove both residual estimates on the whole or any initial part of the step. Discharge L1 and quantify the data.

produces.statement: For every M0>=1,a>=0,0<tau<=1 and smooth real mean-zero f,w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and ||f-w||_2<=1, set q=tau^gamma+||f-w||_2, take Interp_(a,tau;f), and define rho(t)=-integral_a^t B_s(Y,z)ds-(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(Y,Y)ds-((t-a)/tau)W. Then Vst'=(1/2)B_t(Vst,Vst)+rho', rho'=-B_t(Y,z)-(1/2)B_t(Y,Y)-W/tau, sup||rho||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q and ||rho'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

argument.text: Now fix a smooth numerical trajectory and exact twisted v and assume L2: sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), I=[a,b] starts at a grid point, h<=1 and E_I=sup_I||v-V||_2<=1. N007 gives the continuous interpolation V with grid values v^n. Concatenate the residual increments, obtaining Rres and V'=(1/2)B(V,V)+Rres' stepwise and distributionally. At each intersected step start t_n, delta_n=||v^n-v(t_n)||_2=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I, so its q_n<=tau^gamma+E_I and F003 applies with w=v(t_n),f=v^n. There are at most h/tau+1 intersected steps; the last can be partial. Sum the step increment bounds to obtain sup_I||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I). Also sup||Rres'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

produces.statement: Under L2, the accumulated residual bound in the output assertion holds, and ||Rres'||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar)))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

argument.text: Under L2, ||v||_(L^infinity L^2)<=M0 and ||V||_(L^infinity L^2)<=M0+1. Subtract the equations to obtain e'=B_t(e,v-e/2)-Rres'. N005 and F004 imply ||e'||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), so ||e||_X has the same bound. The exact equation bounds ||v'||_(H^(-pstar)), and V=v-e then has bounded X norm too, since tau^gamma+E_I<=2. This proves the remaining assertions. Discharge L2 and quantify the trajectory and interval.

For 0<gamma<=1 set a_gamma=1/2-gamma when gamma<1/2, a_gamma=1/8 when gamma=1/2, and a_gamma=0 when gamma>1/2. Then a_gamma in [0,1), ||f*g||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^(a_gamma)). Constants C_(gamma,M0) below are uniform in a,tau and all higher norms or spectral supports. Then ||f||_2<=M0+1, q<=2, sup_I||F||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0), sup_I||F-Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta, sup_I(||F||_(H^(a_gamma))+||F||_2)<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, ||z||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0), sup_I||B_t(F,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, sup_I||Q||_2+||W||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q, and sup_I||Dinv B_t(f,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Here a_gamma is 1/2-gamma,1/8,0 in the respective cases gamma<1/2, gamma=1/2, gamma>1/2. Moreover Y'=B_t(f,F)+(1/2)B_t(F,F)-W/tau, sup_I||Dinv Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q, sup_I||Dinv Y'||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, Cst(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F(t))-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](f,f,f), sup_I||Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, ||Y||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, and sup_I||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

For 0<gamma<=1, M0>=1, a>=0,0<tau<=1 and smooth mean-zero real f,w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and ||f-w||_2<=1, put q=tau^gamma+||f-w||_2 and take the tuple (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y)=Interp_(a,tau;f); define rho(t)=-integral_a^t B_s(Y,z)ds-(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(Y,Y)ds-((t-a)/tau)*W on [a,a+tau]. Then Vst'=(1/2)B_t(Vst,Vst)+rho', rho'=-B_t(Y,z)-(1/2)B_t(Y,Y)-W/tau, sup||rho||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q, and ||rho'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. On a smooth numerical trajectory and smooth exact twisted solution v with sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, concatenate these increments into Rres(0)=0, and let V be its continuous concatenation with grid values V(t_n)=v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. Then V'=(1/2)B_t(V,V)+Rres'. If I=[a,b] starts at a grid point, h=b-a<=1, e=v-V and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, including an endpoint inside a step, one has sup_(t in I)||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_(X(I))+||V||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0). The constants are independent of grid index, timestep, spectral support and higher norms.

output.statement: Fix 0<gamma<=1 and M0>=1. There exist delta0 in (0,1] and K0>0, depending only on gamma,M0, with the following property. For any 0<tau<=delta0/2, any smooth real mean-zero exact twisted path v satisfying v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, and any smooth real mean-zero numerical trajectory with interpolation V obtained from Interp at its grid values, let e=v-V. On every interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, with h=b-a<=delta0 and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, one has E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma. The endpoint b may lie inside a step. More precisely the proof gives for all N>=2,h<=1,0<tau<=1 under this bootstrap: e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)), F_I(t)=integral_a^t B_s(e,v-e/2)ds; sup_I||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I; F_I=(1/3)[J_s(e,v-e/2)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,v-e/2,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds; sup_I||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I; and E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. Here Rres is the concatenation of the step increments rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,z_n)ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,Y_n)ds-((t-t_n)/tau)W_n, where the subscripted tuple is Interp_(t_n,tau;v^n), with Rres(0)=0, and every constant is independent of time index, timestep, spectral support and higher norms.

locals.declaration: Fix 0<tau<=1, with the smaller final restriction imposed later.
Fix the exact twisted path v.
Fix the interpolation V of the specified numerical trajectory.

argument.text: Assume L1: the smooth real mean-zero v satisfies v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, and the numerical interpolation V is taken on an interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, h<=1, E_I<=1. Set e=v-V,g=v-e/2 and take the concatenated Rres from N009. Its conclusions apply to this trajectory and give the accumulated residual and X bounds. In particular e'=B_t(e,g)-Rres', so integration gives e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)). Also ||e||_X<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||v||_X+||V||_X+||g||_X<=C_(gamma,M0).

produces.statement: Under L1, e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)), sup_I||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_(X(I))+||V||_(X(I))+||g||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0).

argument.text: Fix N>=2 only in the proof. For each time s, the inverse-product bound of N005 and the Fourier inequality ||Ple_N partial_x^2 A||_2<=N^2||A||_2 give ||Ple_N B_s(e,g)||_2<=C*N^2||e||_2||g||_2. Indeed B_s(e,g)=S_(-s)partial_x^2 Dinv P[(S_s e)(S_s g)]. Integrate over length at most h and use bounded ||g||_2 to obtain sup||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1, for every N>=2, sup_I||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I.

argument.text: Apply the two-endpoint normal form N005 to F_I. The equations give e'=B(e,g)-Rres' and g'=(1/2)B(v,v)-(1/2)B(e,g)+(1/2)Rres'. In the differentiated J terms, its symmetry and integral J(B,h)=Ctri give Ctri(e,g,g)-(1/2)Ctri(e,g,e)=Ctri(e,g,V), since g-e/2=V. The other cubic term is (1/2)Ctri(v,v,e), and the forcing terms satisfy -J(Rres',g)+(1/2)J(e,Rres')=-J(Rres',V). Multiplication by -1/3 yields F_I=(1/3)[J_s(e,g)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds. Both endpoints are retained. Apply the H^1 bound for J in N005: their projections above N are <=C_(gamma,M0)*N^(-1)*E_I. Continuity of all the paths makes internal endpoints cancel when the normal form is applied stepwise.

produces.statement: Under L1, F_I(t)=(1/3)[J_s(e,g)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds. The sum of the norms of Pgt_N J_t(e,g) and Pgt_N J_a(e,g) is <=C_(gamma,M0)*N^(-1)*E_I.

argument.text: For any three admissible paths on I, put Lproj=Ple_(N/3),Hproj=I-Lproj. The telescoping expansion Ctri(f_1,f_2,f_3)-Ctri(Lproj f_1,Lproj f_2,Lproj f_3)=Ctri(Hproj f_1,f_2,f_3)+Ctri(Lproj f_1,Hproj f_2,f_3)+Ctri(Lproj f_1,Lproj f_2,Hproj f_3) places a high input in each term. The all-low term has no output above N because all product frequencies sum. Each projection contracts both components of X and ||Hproj f_i||_(H^(-pstar))<=C*N^(-pstar)||f_i||_2 by Fourier weights. Apply N006 with the negative norm on that particular high slot. This proves ||Pgt_N Ctri_I(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C*h*product_j||f_j||_X+C*N^(-pstar)*product_j||f_j||_(L^infinity L^2). Apply this to (e,g,V) and (v,v,e), using F001: their total contribution is <=C_(gamma,M0)*h*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1, ||Pgt_N Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)||_2+||Pgt_N Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*h*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I uniformly for t in I.

argument.text: For the remaining integral in F003 substitute the actual stepwise Rres' formula from N009, and use integral J(B,h)=Ctri from N005 on each intersected step segment. It becomes -Ctri(Y_n,z_n,V)-(1/2)Ctri(Y_n,Y_n,V)-tau^(-1)integral J_s(W_n,V)ds. At that step's start, delta_n=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I. N008 gives ||Y_n||_X<=C*q_n, ||Y_n||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C*tau*q_n, ||z_n||_X<=C and ||W_n||_2<=C*tau*q_n. N006, with the negative norm on Y_n, bounds the first two terms by C*tau*q_n (using q_n<=2 and ||V||_X<=C from F001). The last term is also <=C*tau*q_n by the L^2 J bound from N005. These remain valid upper bounds on a partial final step. At most h/tau+1 steps are met, and q_n<=tau^gamma+E_I. Thus the forcing integral is bounded by C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_(t in I)||integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I). All constants in this bound and the endpoint, cubic, low-frequency and accumulated residual bounds can be dominated by a single positive constant depending only on gamma,M0, uniformly over admissible trajectories, intervals, timesteps and thresholds N>=2.

argument.text: Combine F003-F005 to obtain sup||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. With F002, the exact error identity and residual bound in F001 give E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. All constants are uniform in the parameters specified in F005.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_I||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I, and E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I, with one constant depending only on gamma,M0.

argument.text: Choose C0>=1 dominating these constants from F005-F006, independently of all the particular paths. Define N0=ceil(max(2,16*C0,(16*C0)^(1/pstar))). Then C0*(N0^(-1)+N0^(-pstar))<=1/8<=1/4. Put delta0=min(1,1/(8*C0*(N0^2+3))) and K0=4*C0. If h<=delta0 and tau<=delta0/2, then C0*(N0^2*h+h+tau)<=C0*delta0*(N0^2+3)<=1/8<=1/4. F006 therefore has E_I coefficient at most 1/2. Absorption gives E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+2*C0*(h+tau)*tau^gamma<=2||e(a)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma. These choices depend only on gamma,M0. Discharge L1, retaining its antecedents in the conditional theorem, and quantify all trajectories, intervals and timesteps. This proves the output assertion.

definitions.definition: Torus=R/(2*pi*Z), with measure dx/(2*pi) on [0,2*pi).
For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).

definitions.type: homogeneous Sobolev norms on the mean-zero subspaces

definitions.definition: S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
P0 f=hat f(0), the mean, identified with a constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1); hat(Dinv f)(k)=(i*k)^(-1)hat f(k) for k!=0 and zero for k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). These formulas define maps H^s -> H^(s+1) and H^s -> H^(s+2), respectively.
For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L^2, Ftau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2].

H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
Notation in this copied formula: H_tau=Htau at timestep tau, F_tau=Ftau, P_0=P0, D^(-1)=Dinv and D^(-2)=(Dinv)^2=Dinv2; S_r is the group S at time r. The bracket variable G denotes the entire expression depending on s inside that bracket.

definitions.type: unmodified time-step map and finite numerical trajectories
definitions.definition: Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f), tau>0. For a positive integer Lsteps and tau=T/Lsteps, set t_n=n*tau and u^0=u_0, u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n), 0<=n<Lsteps; v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. No spatial frequency cutoff is applied. This is a finite recursion; its L^2 continuity and preservation properties are proved below.
Ple_N f has coefficients 1_(|k|<=N)*hat f(k), N>=0; Pgt_N=I-Ple_N. These are used only in the proof and in initial-data approximation.
Mavg_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds, tau>0.

definitions.type: average covariance of two exponential phases
definitions.definition:
For real alpha,beta,
M_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds,
eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
The notation M_tau here means Mavg_tau; eta_tau is the family eta at timestep tau.

For tau>0,t0>=0 and mean-zero trigonometric polynomials f_1,f_2,f_3, define hat(Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3))(k)=-tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f_1(a)*hat f_2(b)*hat f_3(c) for k!=0, and zero at k=0. Here p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. The notation R^n_(2,tau) means Rem_(n*tau,tau). The extension to Sobolev inputs is a proved conclusion below, not an assumed estimate. The same Fourier formula defines the operator for smooth inputs by absolutely convergent series: |eta|<=2 from the two averages and smooth Fourier coefficients are rapidly decreasing, so the triple sum is absolutely convergent. The polynomial restriction is its initial dense core.
pstar=23/14.

For an interval I with length at most one, X(I) consists of L^infinity(I;L^2) functions with weak time derivative in L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar)); ||f||_(X(I))=||f||_(L^infinity(I;L^2))+||f'||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar))). All time suprema of continuous functions use their continuous representatives; derivatives and L^infinity norms use essential suprema.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.
J_t(f,g)=S_(-t)P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

Ctri_I(f,g,h)=integral_I S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. For time-independent inputs suppress their t dependence. Initially use smooth spatial inputs, with piecewise smooth continuous time dependence; bounded extensions are justified by the explicit sources or estimates below.
Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/2) integral_a^t B_s(f,g) ds for time-independent smooth mean-zero f,g and a<=t. Fstage_(a,t)(f) abbreviates Fstage_(a,t)(f,f).

For a>=0,tau>0 and smooth mean-zero f, on [a,a+tau] put F(t)=Fstage_(a,t)(f), z(t)=f+F(t), Cst(t)=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s)) ds, Q(t)=(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(F(s),F(s)) ds, W=Q(a+tau)+Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f), Vst(t)=f+F(t)+Cst(t)+Q(t)-((t-a)/tau)*W, Y(t)=Vst(t)-z(t). Interp_(a,tau;f) denotes this entire tuple (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y). It is just these formulas, with no error estimates or endpoint matching granted.

KdV(u;u_0) means u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u_0 on Torus, distributionally. The exact solution sought for real mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation. This predicate itself asserts no existence or quantitative bound.

inputs.statement: 0<gamma<=1.

There is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero datum a0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||a0||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique real mean-zero exact KdV solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma), obtained by smooth approximation, satisfying sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth data have smooth solutions. If a0,b0 are two such data then sup_[0,T]||u_a0(t)-u_b0(t)||_2<=K(T,2*R)||a0-b0||_2. The same estimate holds for any two real mean-zero L^2 data with sum of norms <=2*R. Twisting v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) preserves these bounds; for smooth data v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v). Thus M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma)<=1+A uniformly on the original ball.

For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau is a continuous map on the real mean-zero L^2 space, preserves mean zero and reality, and maps smooth data to smooth data; Ftau:L^2->H^1 is continuous. Hence all finite numerical trajectories are defined and continuous in the initial datum. For every smooth mean-zero real f, tau>0 and integer n>=0, S_(-(n+1)*tau)Psi_tau(S_(n*tau)f)=f+Fstage_(n*tau,(n+1)*tau)(f)+integral_(n*tau)^((n+1)*tau)B_s(f,Fstage_(n*tau,s)(f))ds-Rem_(n*tau,tau)(f,f,f). Consequently on a numerical smooth trajectory the tuple Interp_(t_n,tau;v^n) has Vst(t_n)=v^n and Vst(t_(n+1))=v^(n+1). The interpolants therefore concatenate to a continuous piecewise smooth mean-zero real V on [0,T].

Fix 0<gamma<=1 and M0>=1. There exist delta0 in (0,1] and K0>0, depending only on gamma,M0, with the following property. For any 0<tau<=delta0/2, any smooth real mean-zero exact twisted path v satisfying v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, and any smooth real mean-zero numerical trajectory with interpolation V obtained from Interp at its grid values, let e=v-V. On every interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, with h=b-a<=delta0 and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, one has E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma. The endpoint b may lie inside a step. Let u be its N001 flow, v=S_(-t)u and V the N007 interpolation of the smooth numerical trajectory; e=v-V is continuous and e(0)=0. The common bound is sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=A<M0 and v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v). Put mblock=floor(delta0/tau). Since tau<=delta0/2, mblock>=1 and mblock*tau is in [delta0/2,delta0]. Divide the grid into blocks of mblock steps, with a possibly shorter final block. There are at most Bcount blocks. On each block, or its initial part, on which the bootstrap sup||e||_2<=1 holds, F002 and N010 give E_block<=2||e(start)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma. argument.text: Suppose L2: ||e||_2 reaches 1 somewhere on [0,T]. By continuity and e(0)=0 there is a first such time; the bootstrap is valid up to it. definitions.definition: Torus=R/(2*pi*Z), with measure dx/(2*pi) on [0,2*pi).
For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).

definitions.definition: S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
P0 f=hat f(0), the mean, identified with a constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1); hat(Dinv f)(k)=(i*k)^(-1)hat f(k) for k!=0 and zero for k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). These formulas define maps H^s -> H^(s+1) and H^s -> H^(s+2), respectively.
For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L^2, Ftau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2].

H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
Notation in this copied formula: H_tau=Htau at timestep tau, F_tau=Ftau, P_0=P0, D^(-1)=Dinv and D^(-2)=(Dinv)^2=Dinv2; S_r is the group S at time r. The bracket variable G denotes the entire expression depending on s inside that bracket.

definitions.definition: Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f), tau>0. For a positive integer Lsteps and tau=T/Lsteps, set t_n=n*tau and u^0=u_0, u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n), 0<=n<Lsteps; v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. No spatial frequency cutoff is applied. This is a finite recursion; its L^2 continuity and preservation properties are proved below.
Ple_N f has coefficients 1_(|k|<=N)*hat f(k), N>=0; Pgt_N=I-Ple_N. These are used only in the proof and in initial-data approximation.
Mavg_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds, tau>0.

definitions.definition:
For real alpha,beta,
M_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds,
eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
The notation M_tau here means Mavg_tau; eta_tau is the family eta at timestep tau.

For tau>0,t0>=0 and mean-zero trigonometric polynomials f_1,f_2,f_3, define hat(Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3))(k)=-tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f_1(a)*hat f_2(b)*hat f_3(c) for k!=0, and zero at k=0. Here p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. The notation R^n_(2,tau) means Rem_(n*tau,tau). The extension to Sobolev inputs is a proved conclusion below, not an assumed estimate. The same Fourier formula defines the operator for smooth inputs by absolutely convergent series: |eta|<=2 from the two averages and smooth Fourier coefficients are rapidly decreasing, so the triple sum is absolutely convergent. The polynomial restriction is its initial dense core.
pstar=23/14.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.
Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/2) integral_a^t B_s(f,g) ds for time-independent smooth mean-zero f,g and a<=t. Fstage_(a,t)(f) abbreviates Fstage_(a,t)(f,f).

For a>=0,tau>0 and smooth mean-zero f, on [a,a+tau] put F(t)=Fstage_(a,t)(f), z(t)=f+F(t), Cst(t)=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s)) ds, Q(t)=(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(F(s),F(s)) ds, W=Q(a+tau)+Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f), Vst(t)=f+F(t)+Cst(t)+Q(t)-((t-a)/tau)*W, Y(t)=Vst(t)-z(t). This predicate itself asserts no existence or quantitative bound.

original_context.full_target:
Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with the standing definitions of Section 2 of the supplied paper.

Use normalized measure dx/(2*pi) on the torus \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/(2*pi \mathbb{Z}). The Fourier coefficient is
\hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx,
and ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2s)|\hat f(k)|^2, where <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2).
These spaces are the completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms; negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. The normalized L^2 norm is the s=0 norm. For mean-zero functions, the homogeneous norm uses |k|^(2s) in place of <k>^(2s). For s>=0,
||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s);
for s<0, 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=||f||_(dot H^s).
Real-valued means \hat f(-k)=overline(\hat f(k)), and mean-zero means \hat f(0)=0.
All time suprema concern continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

Let S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), so \widehat{S_t f}(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)\hat f(k).
Let P_0 be the mean and P=I-P_0. Let D^(-1)=partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k!=0 and zero at k=0; D^(-2)=(D^(-1))^2.
The equation is
u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2),  u(0)=u_0. [Eq. (1)]
The exact solution u is the unique real, mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation and satisfies this equation distributionally.

For a positive integer L and tau=T/L, the fixed time-semidiscrete scheme is u^0=u_0 and
u^(n+1)=S_tau u^n+F_tau(u^n)+H_tau(u^n), 0<=n<L, [Eq. (2)]
where
F_tau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(D^(-1)f)^2],
H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
This is the fixed scheme of the paper's reference [1, Eq. (1.4)], without a spatial frequency cutoff.

For every T>0, every 0<gamma<=1 and every R>0, there exist C>0 and tau_0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real, mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma(\mathbb{T}) with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau_0, this exact fixed scheme satisfies
max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2)<=C*tau^gamma.
The same C and tau_0 apply to the entire stated initial-data ball; no spectral support bound or additional smoothness is a hypothesis.

In the source's standing notation v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) and M=1+sup_(0<=t<=T)||v(t)||_(H^gamma).
Constants C_M may vary from line to line and depend on gamma,T,M, but are uniform in n,tau and spectral support. Section 2.1 supplies M<=1+A(T,gamma,R) uniformly on the ball using the cited exact-flow results; it is not an extra hypothesis on u_0. The source uses the continuous estimates from [1, Proposition 3.4 and Lemma 7.2] and does not use the logarithmic convergence theorem as an input.

Apply it to S_t Dinv f and S_t Dinv g and use S_t isometric and P contractive to obtain ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. Each assertion is quantified over inputs in its indicated space.

value.text: For L^2 f,g, every Fourier coefficient of the product (S_t f)(S_t g) has modulus <=||f||_2||g||_2 by Cauchy-Schwarz in the convolution. Hence ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))^2<=||f||_2^2||g||_2^2 sum_(k!=0) k^2<k>^(-2*pstar), a finite sum because pstar=23/14>3/2. The same coefficient bound with sum k^(-2) proves ||Dinv P(f*g)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A0, <k>^(-pstar)<=|k|^(-1), so ||A0||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A0||_2. Finally J_t(A0,g) is a product of S_t Dinv A0 in L^2 and S_t Dinv g in L^infinity, followed by contractions, so its L^2 norm is <=C||Dinv A0||_2||g||_2 by F001. Approximation by polynomials and these continuous bilinear bounds justify the products and their extensions.

produces.statement: For L^2 f,g, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2 and ||Dinv P(f*g)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A0 with Dinv A0 in L^2, ||A0||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A0||_2 and ||J_t(A0,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A0||_2||g||_2.

value.text: For the normal-form clause take smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b]. At k!=0 the coefficient of J_t is sum_(r+s=k) exp(-i*t*3*k*r*s)*(i*r)^(-1)*(i*s)^(-1)*hat f(r)*hat g(s). Differentiating the phase gives 3*i*k times the product coefficients. Therefore d_t J_t(f,g)=3*B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Smooth spatial Fourier series and all derivatives used here converge absolutely, so differentiation and integration are legitimate. Integration gives the displayed two-endpoint normal form. For piecewise smooth continuous paths apply this on each subinterval; intermediate J endpoint values cancel because the paths are continuous.

produces.statement: For smooth or continuous piecewise smooth mean-zero paths f,g, integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt.

value.text: Symmetry of J is immediate from the product formula. Since Dinv partial_x=P, substitution gives J_t(B_t(f,g),h)=S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f)(S_t g)]*(S_t Dinv h)}, whose integral on I is exactly Ctri_I(f,g,h); no inverse derivative is commuted through a product. For constant f,g, integrate F003 and multiply by 1/2 to obtain Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/6)[J_s(f,g)]_a^t. This establishes every identity asserted in the output assertion.

original_context.full_target:
Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with the standing definitions of Section 2 of the supplied paper.

Use normalized measure dx/(2*pi) on the torus \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/(2*pi \mathbb{Z}). The Fourier coefficient is
\hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx,
and ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2s)|\hat f(k)|^2, where <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2).
These spaces are the completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms; negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. The normalized L^2 norm is the s=0 norm. For mean-zero functions, the homogeneous norm uses |k|^(2s) in place of <k>^(2s). For s>=0,
||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s);
for s<0, 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=||f||_(dot H^s).
Real-valued means \hat f(-k)=overline(\hat f(k)), and mean-zero means \hat f(0)=0.
All time suprema concern continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

Let S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), so \widehat{S_t f}(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)\hat f(k).
Let P_0 be the mean and P=I-P_0. Let D^(-1)=partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k!=0 and zero at k=0; D^(-2)=(D^(-1))^2.
The equation is
u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2),  u(0)=u_0. [Eq. (1)]
The exact solution u is the unique real, mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation and satisfies this equation distributionally.

For a positive integer L and tau=T/L, the fixed time-semidiscrete scheme is u^0=u_0 and
u^(n+1)=S_tau u^n+F_tau(u^n)+H_tau(u^n), 0<=n<L, [Eq. (2)]
where
F_tau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(D^(-1)f)^2],
H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
This is the fixed scheme of the paper's reference [1, Eq. (1.4)], without a spatial frequency cutoff.

For every T>0, every 0<gamma<=1 and every R>0, there exist C>0 and tau_0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real, mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma(\mathbb{T}) with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau_0, this exact fixed scheme satisfies
max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2)<=C*tau^gamma.
The same C and tau_0 apply to the entire stated initial-data ball; no spectral support bound or additional smoothness is a hypothesis.

In the source's standing notation v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) and M=1+sup_(0<=t<=T)||v(t)||_(H^gamma).
Constants C_M may vary from line to line and depend on gamma,T,M, but are uniform in n,tau and spectral support. Section 2.1 supplies M<=1+A(T,gamma,R) uniformly on the ball using the cited exact-flow results; it is not an extra hypothesis on u_0. The source uses the continuous estimates from [1, Proposition 3.4 and Lemma 7.2] and does not use the logarithmic convergence theorem as an input.

definitions.definition: Torus=ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), with measure dx/(2*pi) on [0,2*pi). Here ℝ denotes the real number system, distinct from the radius parameter R.
For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).

definitions.type: homogeneous Sobolev norms on the mean-zero subspaces

definitions.definition: S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
pstar=23/14.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.

KdV(u;u_0) means u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u_0 on Torus, distributionally. The exact solution sought for real mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation. This predicate itself asserts no existence or quantitative bound.

inputs.statement: 0<gamma<=1.

For the real mean-zero periodic equation U_t=U*U_x+U_xxx on ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), use hat U(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral U(x)exp(-i*k*x)dx, ||U||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2s)|hat U(k)|^2, and z_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t)hat U(t)(k). For every s>0 and horizon Q>0, every initial datum U_0 in dot H^s has a distributional solution with z in C([0,Q];dot H^s), unique in the source solution class (z in L^infinity dot H^0 satisfying z_k(t)-z_k(0)=(i*k/2)integral_0^t sum_(k1+k2=k)exp(i*3*k*k1*k2*r)z_k1(r)z_k2(r)dr). Its dot H^0 norm is conserved, and the flow depends Lipschitz continuously on the initial data in dot H^s, uniformly on bounded dot H^s sets on [0,Q]. The Galerkin approximations (with the nonlinear inputs and output projected to |k|<=m and high coefficients frozen) have dot H^s bounds uniform in m, depending only on s,Q, the initial dot H^s norm and an upper bound for the initial dot H^0 norm. For 0<sigma<s they admit a subsequence converging strongly in L^q([0,Q];dot H^sigma), 1<q<infinity, and weak-* in L^infinity dot H^s to this solution; the same dot H^s bound holds for the limit. For s=0 there is a unique C([0,Q];dot H^0) solution, conserving that norm and depending Lipschitz continuously on its data. These flows agree on overlapping regularity classes and are obtained by smooth approximation.

The horizon Q is positive and the nonnegative Sobolev regularity and initial norms are as stated.

inputs.statement: For Q>0, theta in (-1,0] and real mean-zero initial data U_0,W_0 in dot H^0 with ||U_0||_(dot H^0)+||W_0||_(dot H^0)<=B0, the two source twisted solutions z,y of z_k'=(i*k/2)sum_(k1+k2=k) exp(i*3*k*k1*k2*t)z_k1*z_k2 with these initial coefficients satisfy sup_(0<=t<=Q)||z(t)-y(t)||_(dot H^theta)<=C'(B0,theta)*C_(B0,theta)^Q*||U_0-W_0||_(dot H^theta). output.statement: There is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero datum a0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||a0||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique real mean-zero exact KdV solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma), obtained by smooth approximation, satisfying sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth data have smooth solutions. If a0,b0 are two such data then sup_[0,T]||u_a0(t)-u_b0(t)||_2<=K(T,2*R)||a0-b0||_2. The same estimate holds for any two real mean-zero L^2 data with sum of norms <=2*R. Twisting v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) preserves these bounds; for smooth data v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v). Thus M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma)<=1+A uniformly on the original ball.

locals.declaration: Choose the source solution U with initial datum U0, whose existence is F001.
Fix a second datum b0 for the pairwise L^2 assertion.

argument.text: H001-H003 give T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0. Fix a0 and temporarily assume L1: a0 is real, mean-zero, in H^gamma and ||a0||_(H^gamma)<=R. Set U0(x)=-a0(-x), so hat U0(k)=-hat a0(-k). It is real and mean-zero and preserves all Fourier Sobolev norms. In particular ||U0||_(dot H^gamma)<=R and ||U0||_2<=R. Apply E001 with s=gamma,Q=T,U_0=U0. Its hypotheses hold by these norm facts and H001-H002. It supplies a unique continuous source flow U, a uniform homogeneous bound depending only on T,gamma,R, and smooth-approximation construction. Record its existence as F001.

produces.statement: There exists the unique source solution with initial datum U0 on [0,T], continuous in dot H^gamma, bounded there by a constant depending only on T,gamma,R, constructed by smooth approximation.

argument.text: Choose U from F001 and set u(t,x)=-U(t,-x). For smooth solutions u_t=-U_t, u_x=U_x and u_xxx=U_xxx at (t,-x), so u_t+u_xxx=-UU_x=u*u_x=(1/2)partial_x(u^2). The same equality follows distributionally by the reflection change of variables for the limiting solution. Fourier coefficients satisfy hat u(t)(k)=-hat U(t)(-k), hence all Sobolev norms, zero mean and reality are preserved. The comparison ||u||_(H^gamma)<=2^(gamma/2)||U||_(dot H^gamma) gives a bound A(T,gamma,R). Finite Fourier norm sums pass to the limit under smooth approximation, and their supremum gives the full bound; continuity gives it for every time. Uniqueness follows by applying the inverse reflection to two solutions, using the source coefficient formulation, equivalent to the distributional equation for continuous L^2 paths by testing each Fourier mode. Set v=S_(-t)u. Unit-modulus multipliers preserve its H^gamma norm. Differentiation for smooth data gives v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v).

produces.statement: Under L1 the exact u exists uniquely, sup_[0,T]||u||_(H^gamma)<=A(T,gamma,R), v=S_(-t)u has the same bound, and for smooth data v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v).

argument.text: For the smooth-data clause, temporarily assume L3: a0 is smooth. Apply E001 at every positive integer regularity s, with this same U0. Its finite higher norms and uniqueness make all these solutions coincide with U. Thus u is spatially smooth, and the equation supplies its time smoothness. Discharge L3 to obtain that conditional clause, and discharge L1 to obtain the stated assertion for every a0 in the ball. For the pairwise assertion fix arbitrary a0,b0 and temporarily assume L2: they are real mean-zero L^2 data whose norms sum to at most 2*R. Define W0=-b0(-x). E001 with s=0,Q=T supplies the source L^2 flows for each of U0,W0. Apply E002 with Q=T,theta=0,B0=2*R to those flows. Their zero mean, reality and norm sum are unchanged by reflection; theta=0 lies in (-1,0]. Its source common untwisting multiplier is an L^2 isometry, so E002 and reflection give sup||u_a0-u_b0||_2<=K(T,2*R)||a0-b0||_2. This includes the original H^gamma ball since each norm is <=R. Discharge L2. The constructions and bounds hold for every chosen datum; M=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=1+A. This proves the output assertion.

definitions.definition:
For real alpha,beta,
M_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds,
eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
The notation M_tau here means Mavg_tau; eta_tau is the family eta at timestep tau.

output.statement: For every tau>0 and alpha,beta in ℝ, eta_tau(alpha,beta)=0 if alpha*beta=0. Otherwise |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=2*min(|alpha/beta|,|beta/alpha|) and |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=tau*min(|alpha|,|beta|).

argument.text: Fix tau>0, alpha,beta real. If either phase vanishes its exponential is 1 and the covariance is zero. In the remaining case assume L1: alpha*beta!=0. Define h(s)=exp(-i*alpha*s)-Mavg_tau(exp(-i*alpha*.)). Then eta=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau h(s)exp(-i*beta*s)ds. The elementary integral estimate |exp(-i*alpha*s)-exp(-i*alpha*r)|<=|alpha||s-r| gives |h(s)|<=tau^(-1)integral_0^tau |alpha||s-r|dr<=tau|alpha|. Consequently |eta|<=tau|alpha|. At s=0,tau the sharper integrals are each tau|alpha|/2, so |h(0)|+|h(tau)|<=tau|alpha|; also integral_0^tau|h'(s)|ds=tau|alpha|.

produces.statement: Under L1, |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=tau|alpha| and |h(0)|+|h(tau)|+integral_0^tau|h'|<=2*tau|alpha|.

argument.text: Integration by parts against exp(-i*beta*s), which has nonzero derivative factor -i*beta under L1, gives |eta|<= (|h(0)|+|h(tau)|+integral|h'|)/(tau|beta|)<=2|alpha/beta| by F001. The defining covariance is symmetric in alpha,beta; repeating both estimates with the phases interchanged gives |eta|<=tau|beta| and |eta|<=2|beta/alpha|. Take their minima, discharge L1, and include the zero-phase case already calculated. Universal introduction proves the output assertion.
