argument.text: For the pointwise assertions fix integers a,b,c,d and assume L1: abcd!=0 and a+b+c+d=0. Order their magnitudes as N1>=N2>=N3>=N4. The largest is bounded by the sum of the other three, so N1<=3*N2. Put A0=|ab|, B0=|cd|. If d is among the two largest, min(A0/B0,B0/A0)<=1 and 1/|d|<=1/N3. If not, the largest two are among a,b,c. If they are a,b, use B0/A0 to bound the desired expression by |c|/|ab|<=1/N3. If they are a,c, their ratio lies in [1/3,3]. Therefore the expression is at most 3*min(|b|/|d|^2,1/|b|)<=3/max(|b|,|d|)=3/N3: use the first alternative if |d|>=|b| and the second otherwise. The case b,c is identical after swapping a,b. This proves the first majorant.

produces.statement: Under L1, N1<=3*N2 and (1/|d|)min(A0/B0,B0/A0)<=3/N3.

argument.text: For the second majorant, if the two largest are in the same pair of (a,b),(c,d), the other pair sums to magnitude at most 2*N3. Since a+b=-(c+d), |a+b|/max(A0,B0)<=2*N3/(N1*N2)<=2/N3. If they lie in different pairs, the third largest is paired with one of them, whence max(A0,B0)>=N2*N3; also |a+b|<=2*N1<=6*N2 by F001. The quotient is <=6/N3. Any ordering of ties is covered. Discharge L1; these are the claimed conditional pointwise statements for all such frequencies.

Fix four nonnegative ell^2 sequences x_r. First restrict all of them to finitely many frequencies. Decompose each into shells 2^j<=|k|<2^(j+1), j>=0, and let Xshell_(r,j) be its ell^2 norm there. Fix one of the at most 24 orderings of the four shell indices j1>=j2>=j3>=j4, permuting the sequence labels accordingly. A nonzero zero-sum interaction requires j1-j2<=2, since otherwise the largest magnitude would exceed the sum of the other three. For each fixed pair of the two smaller frequencies, sum the two larger-frequency sequences subject to their prescribed sum. Cauchy-Schwarz, applied to a translated reflection, bounds that sum by their shell ell^2 norm product. A shell contains at most 2^(j+1) integers, so summing each smaller sequence in ell^1 costs at most C*2^(j/2) times its ell^2 norm. Thus the shell contribution without the weight is <=C*2^((j3+j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr). On that shell N3>=2^j3, so the weight leaves C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2).

produces.statement: For every ordered four-shell zero-sum interaction j1>=j2>=j3>=j4, its weighted contribution is <=C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr), and j1-j2 is in {0,1,2}.

argument.text: For each q in {0,1,2}, set j1=J,j2=J-q. Drop the upper restrictions on the smaller shells; nonnegativity increases the sum. F002 bounds the ordered contribution by C*(sum_J Xshell_(1,J)*Xshell_(2,J-q))*(sum_(ell>=m>=0)2^(-(ell-m)/2)*Xshell_(3,ell)*Xshell_(4,m)). The first factor is at most ||Xshell_1||_ell2||Xshell_2||_ell2. Set r=ell-m; for each r the second correlation is at most ||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2 by Cauchy-Schwarz, so the second factor is at most sum_(r>=0)2^(-r/2)||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2=||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2/(1-2^(-1/2)). Shell disjointness identifies each shell-norm ell^2 norm with ||x_r||_ell2. Sum over 24 orderings and three offsets. This proves the finite bound with an absolute constant.

produces.statement: For the finite restrictions of the current nonnegative ell^2 sequences, sum_(a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0)x_1(a)x_2(b)x_3(c)x_4(d)/N3(a,b,c,d)<=C*product_(r=1)^4||x_r||_ell2, with absolute C independent of the supports; N3 is the third largest magnitude in the summand.

argument.text: For arbitrary nonnegative ell^2 sequences restrict all inputs to |k|<=m and apply F003. Their norms are bounded by the full norms. Every finite subset of interactions is included in some such restriction, so the infinite positive sum, defined as the supremum over finite subsums, has the same bound. Restricting to any subset only decreases that nonnegative sum. Together with the pointwise assertions this proves the output assertion without exchanging conditionally convergent sums.

For real alpha,beta,
M_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds,
eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).

definitions.definition: For tau>0,t0>=0 and mean-zero trigonometric polynomials f_1,f_2,f_3, define hat(Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3))(k)=-tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f_1(a)*hat f_2(b)*hat f_3(c) for k!=0, and zero at k=0. Here p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. The notation R^n_(2,tau) means Rem_(n*tau,tau). The extension to Sobolev inputs is a proved conclusion below, not an assumed estimate. The same Fourier formula defines the operator for smooth inputs by absolutely convergent series: |eta|<=2 from the two averages and smooth Fourier coefficients are rapidly decreasing, so the triple sum is absolutely convergent. The polynomial restriction is its initial dense core.

In the nonzero interaction a+b+c=k, d=-k, the multiplier obeys |eta_tau(3ab(a+b),3kc(a+b))|/(|k||abc|^sigma)<=6^(1-sigma)*18^sigma*tau^sigma/N3(a,b,c,-k). The same estimates hold with any additional interaction multiplier of modulus <=1, including restrictions to Phi=0 or Phi!=0. In particular if 0<sigma<=1, 0<tau<=1, w in mean-zero H^sigma, f in mean-zero L^2, ||w||_(H^sigma)<=M0 and delta=||f-w||_2<=1, then ||Rem_(t0,tau)(f,f,f)||_2<=C_(sigma,M0)*tau*(tau^sigma+delta), with no Sobolev hypothesis on f.

argument.text: Fix sigma,tau,t0 and polynomial inputs. In each nonzero term write k=a+b+c, p=a+b, d=-k, A0=|ab|,B0=|cd|, and let N3 be the third largest of |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|. Terms with a zero input frequency, zero k, or zero phase vanish by definition and N002. On the remaining terms alpha=3abp,beta=3kcp. The ratio bound of N002 and the first majorant of N003 give |eta|/|k|<=6/N3. The small-phase bound gives |eta|/(tau|abck|)<=3|p|min(A0,B0)/(A0*B0)=3|p|/max(A0,B0)<=18/N3 by N003. Their geometric interpolation with weights 1-sigma,sigma yields |eta|/(|k||abc|^sigma)<=6^(1-sigma)18^sigma*tau^sigma/N3. This includes sigma=0 and sigma=1 as the separate endpoint bounds.

produces.statement: For all nonzero integers a,b,c,k with a+b+c=k and a+b!=0, put N3=third-largest(|a|,|b|,|c|,|k|). Then |eta_tau(3ab(a+b),3kc(a+b))|/(|k||abc|^sigma)<=6^(1-sigma)*18^sigma*tau^sigma/N3. Zero-phase terms vanish. The estimate includes sigma=0 and sigma=1.

argument.text: Dualize the Fourier coefficients of Rem against a finitely supported unit ell^2 sequence. After absolute values, use F001 and N003 with x_1(a)=|a|^sigma|hat f_1(a)| and likewise for slots 2 and 3; take x_4(d) to be the modulus of the dual coefficient at -d. Their norms are bounded by the three H^sigma norms and the unit dual norm. The factor exp(-i*t0*Phi) has modulus one, and the prefactor in Rem is tau/18. Thus ||Rem||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)product_j||f_j||_(H^sigma). A multiplier of modulus <=1 only decreases the absolute majorant, so the same proof covers every stated restriction.

produces.statement: For the mean-zero polynomial inputs, ||Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product_(j=1)^3||f_j||_(H^sigma), uniformly in their supports, t0 and tau, including any fixed interaction multiplier of modulus <=1.

argument.text: Approximate each mean-zero H^sigma input by its finite Fourier projections. The trilinear bound F002 and the three-term telescoping difference bound show that the outputs are Cauchy in the complete L^2 space, independently of the chosen approximations. This defines a unique bounded trilinear extension and retains the inequality. For smooth inputs it coincides with the original absolutely convergent Fourier expression. At sigma=0 this supplies in particular an L^2-by-L^2-by-L^2 bound C*tau.

produces.statement: For every exponent rho in [0,1], Rem_(t0,tau) has a unique bounded trilinear extension to the mean-zero H^rho inputs g_1,g_2,g_3, with ||Rem_(t0,tau)(g_1,g_2,g_3)||_2<=C_rho*tau^(1+rho)*product_j||g_j||_(H^rho). The same bound holds with any fixed extra multiplier of modulus <=1, and at rho=0 it is C*tau times the product of L^2 norms.

argument.text: For the final clause fix f,w,M0 and temporarily assume L1: 0<sigma<=1,0<tau<=1,w in mean-zero H^sigma with ||w||_(H^sigma)<=M0, f in mean-zero L^2, and delta=||f-w||_2<=1. Apply F003 with exponent sigma to (w,w,w). Expand Rem(f,f,f)-Rem(w,w,w) as Rem(f-w,f,f)+Rem(w,f-w,f)+Rem(w,w,f-w) and apply F003 with exponent zero to each term. The difference is bounded by C*tau*delta*(||f||_2+||w||_2)^2. Since ||f||_2<=M0+1, this yields C_(sigma,M0)*tau*(tau^sigma+delta). Discharge L1 and quantify all data. This proves the output assertion.

S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
P0 f=hat f(0), the mean, identified with a constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1); hat(Dinv f)(k)=(i*k)^(-1)hat f(k) for k!=0 and zero for k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). These formulas define maps H^s -> H^(s+1) and H^s -> H^(s+2), respectively.
pstar=23/14.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.
J_t(f,g)=S_(-t)P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

Ctri_I(f,g,h)=integral_I S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. For time-independent inputs suppress their t dependence. Initially use smooth spatial inputs, with piecewise smooth continuous time dependence; bounded extensions are justified by the explicit sources or estimates below.
Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/2) integral_a^t B_s(f,g) ds for time-independent smooth mean-zero f,g and a<=t. Fstage_(a,t)(f) abbreviates Fstage_(a,t)(f,f).

output.statement: The following estimates have constants uniform in the real time t. For mean-zero f in L^2, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2. For any A0,B0 in H^1, ||A0*B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1). For f,g in L^2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(f*g)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A0 with Dinv A0 in L^2 and g in L^2, ||A0||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A0||_2 and ||J_t(A0,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A0||_2||g||_2. For smooth mean-zero time-dependent f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. J is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=Ctri_I(f,g,h). These identities hold piecewise and sum across internal endpoints for continuous piecewise smooth paths. For time-independent mean-zero f,g, Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/6)[J_s(f,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t). The bounded products extend from polynomials by density.

For a general H^1 function its mean plus this estimate for its derivative gives ||A0||_infinity<=C||A0||_(H^1). The product rule then gives ||A0*B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1). Apply it to S_t Dinv f and S_t Dinv g and use S_t isometric and P contractive to obtain ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. Each assertion is quantified over inputs in its indicated space.

argument.text: For L^2 f,g, every Fourier coefficient of the product (S_t f)(S_t g) has modulus <=||f||_2||g||_2 by Cauchy-Schwarz in the convolution. Hence ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))^2<=||f||_2^2||g||_2^2 sum_(k!=0) k^2<k>^(-2*pstar), a finite sum because pstar=23/14>3/2. The same coefficient bound with sum k^(-2) proves ||Dinv P(f*g)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A0, <k>^(-pstar)<=|k|^(-1), so ||A0||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A0||_2. Finally J_t(A0,g) is a product of S_t Dinv A0 in L^2 and S_t Dinv g in L^infinity, followed by contractions, so its L^2 norm is <=C||Dinv A0||_2||g||_2 by F001. Approximation by polynomials and these continuous bilinear bounds justify the products and their extensions.

produces.statement: For L^2 f,g, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2 and ||Dinv P(f*g)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A0 with Dinv A0 in L^2, ||A0||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A0||_2 and ||J_t(A0,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A0||_2||g||_2.

argument.text: For the normal-form clause take smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b]. At k!=0 the coefficient of J_t is sum_(r+s=k) exp(-i*t*3*k*r*s)*(i*r)^(-1)*(i*s)^(-1)*hat f(r)*hat g(s). Differentiating the phase gives 3*i*k times the product coefficients. Therefore d_t J_t(f,g)=3*B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Smooth spatial Fourier series and all derivatives used here converge absolutely, so differentiation and integration are legitimate. Integration gives the displayed two-endpoint normal form. For piecewise smooth continuous paths apply this on each subinterval; intermediate J endpoint values cancel because the paths are continuous.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. argument.text: Fix tau>0. N005 makes Dinv:L^2->H^1 bounded and H^1 an algebra. Therefore Ftau is a continuous quadratic map L^2->H^1. In Htau the first product has factors S_tau Dinv f and Dinv Ftau(f) in H^1; the second uses the continuous bilinear mean P0(f^2) and S_tau Dinv f; the third is an H^1 cube followed by Dinv and S; the fourth multiplies S_(s-tau)Dinv2 Ftau(f) by S_s Dinv f in H^1, followed by Dinv2 and S, evaluated at two endpoints. Every coefficient, including 1/tau, is finite at this fixed tau. Hence all four terms, Ftau and Psi_tau are continuous in L^2. Fourier conjugate symmetry is preserved by S, Dinv, products and real coefficients. Every projected or inverse-derivative term has zero mean, and the unprojected second term of Htau is a scalar times the mean-zero S_tau Dinv f. Thus the update is real and mean-zero. The same formulas preserve spatial smoothness. Finite induction gives the asserted well-defined finite trajectories and continuous dependence at fixed tau.

produces.statement: For each fixed tau>0 the full update Psi_tau is continuous on real mean-zero L^2, preserves that subspace and smoothness, and Ftau maps continuously to H^1.

argument.text: For the endpoint identity now take smooth real mean-zero f and integer n>=0. Apply E006 with precisely this f,n,tau. Its exponential convention agrees with S_(-t), and its F^n and A^n are respectively Fstage and the displayed B integral; its R_2^n is D015 with t0=n*tau. This gives exactly the asserted twisted update. There is no norm conversion in this algebraic identity.

produces.statement: For tau>0, n>=0 integer, t_n=n*tau and a smooth real mean-zero f, let uold=S_(t_n)f and unew=Psi_tau(uold), with the displayed unfiltered update. Then S_(-(t_n+tau))unew=f+Fstage_(t_n,t_n+tau)(f)+integral_(t_n)^(t_n+tau) B_s(f,Fstage_(t_n,s)(f)) ds-Rem_(t_n,tau)(f,f,f).

argument.text: At t=t_n, all stage integrals in Interp vanish and its affine correction is zero, so Vst(t_n)=f. At t=t_n+tau, Q(t) cancels its contribution to W and Vst=f+Fstage+Cst-Rem. With f=v^n, F002 identifies this as v^(n+1). F001 ensures the next state remains smooth and real mean-zero. Thus adjacent pieces have matching endpoints, and the concatenation is continuous and piecewise smooth, real and mean-zero. This proves the output assertion.

definitions.definition: Torus=ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), with measure dx/(2*pi) on [0,2*pi). Here ℝ denotes the real number system, distinct from the radius parameter R.
For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).
S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
P0 f=hat f(0), the mean, identified with a constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1); hat(Dinv f)(k)=(i*k)^(-1)hat f(k) for k!=0 and zero for k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). These formulas define maps H^s -> H^(s+1) and H^s -> H^(s+2), respectively.
Mavg_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds, tau>0.

definitions.type: average covariance of two exponential phases
definitions.definition:
For real alpha,beta,
M_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds,
eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
The notation M_tau here means Mavg_tau; eta_tau is the family eta at timestep tau.

definitions.definition: For tau>0,t0>=0 and mean-zero trigonometric polynomials f_1,f_2,f_3, define hat(Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3))(k)=-tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f_1(a)*hat f_2(b)*hat f_3(c) for k!=0, and zero at k=0. Here p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. The notation R^n_(2,tau) means Rem_(n*tau,tau). The extension to Sobolev inputs is a proved conclusion below, not an assumed estimate. The same Fourier formula defines the operator for smooth inputs by absolutely convergent series: |eta|<=2 from the two averages and smooth Fourier coefficients are rapidly decreasing, so the triple sum is absolutely convergent. The polynomial restriction is its initial dense core.
pstar=23/14.

For an interval I with length at most one, X(I) consists of L^infinity(I;L^2) functions with weak time derivative in L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar)); ||f||_(X(I))=||f||_(L^infinity(I;L^2))+||f'||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar))). All time suprema of continuous functions use their continuous representatives; derivatives and L^infinity norms use essential suprema.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.
J_t(f,g)=S_(-t)P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

Ctri_I(f,g,h)=integral_I S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. For time-independent inputs suppress their t dependence. Initially use smooth spatial inputs, with piecewise smooth continuous time dependence; bounded extensions are justified by the explicit sources or estimates below.
Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/2) integral_a^t B_s(f,g) ds for time-independent smooth mean-zero f,g and a<=t. Fstage_(a,t)(f) abbreviates Fstage_(a,t)(f,f).

For a>=0,tau>0 and smooth mean-zero f, on [a,a+tau] put F(t)=Fstage_(a,t)(f), z(t)=f+F(t), Cst(t)=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s)) ds, Q(t)=(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(F(s),F(s)) ds, W=Q(a+tau)+Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f), Vst(t)=f+F(t)+Cst(t)+Q(t)-((t-a)/tau)*W, Y(t)=Vst(t)-z(t). Interp_(a,tau;f) denotes this entire tuple (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y). It is just these formulas, with no error estimates or endpoint matching granted.

inputs.statement: 0<gamma<=1.

For every 0<=sigma<=1, tau>0, t0>=0 and mean-zero f_j in H^sigma, Rem_(t0,tau) has a unique bounded trilinear extension with ||Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product_j||f_j||_(H^sigma), uniformly in t0,tau and Fourier support. In the nonzero interaction a+b+c=k, d=-k, the multiplier obeys |eta_tau(3ab(a+b),3kc(a+b))|/(|k||abc|^sigma)<=6^(1-sigma)*18^sigma*tau^sigma/N3(a,b,c,-k). The same estimates hold with any additional interaction multiplier of modulus <=1, including restrictions to Phi=0 or Phi!=0. In particular if 0<sigma<=1, 0<tau<=1, w in mean-zero H^sigma, f in mean-zero L^2, ||w||_(H^sigma)<=M0 and delta=||f-w||_2<=1, then ||Rem_(t0,tau)(f,f,f)||_2<=C_(sigma,M0)*tau*(tau^sigma+delta), with no Sobolev hypothesis on f.

The following estimates have constants uniform in the real time t. For mean-zero f in L^2, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2. For any A0,B0 in H^1, ||A0*B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1). For f,g in L^2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(f*g)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A0 with Dinv A0 in L^2 and g in L^2, ||A0||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A0||_2 and ||J_t(A0,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A0||_2||g||_2. The bounded products extend from polynomials by density.

Then ||f||_2<=M0+1, q<=2, sup_I||F||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0), sup_I||F-Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta, sup_I(||F||_(H^(a_gamma))+||F||_2)<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, ||z||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0), sup_I||B_t(F,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, sup_I||Q||_2+||W||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q, and sup_I||Dinv B_t(f,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. argument.text: Fix the local a,tau,M0,f,w, and assume L1: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and delta=||f-w||_2<=1. H002 gives 0<gamma<=1, hence q=tau^gamma+delta<=2 and ||f||_2<=M0+1. Take the tuple from Interp and the exponent a_gamma from N006. By the endpoint formula in N005, F(t)=(1/6)[J_s(f,f)]_a^t. The J:H^0 times H^0->H^1 bound gives sup||F||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0). Expanding J(f,f)-J(w,w) as J(f-w,f)+J(w,f-w) gives sup||F-Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta. Since a_gamma<1, N006 now yields sup(||F||_(H^(a_gamma))+||F||_2)<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Also z=f+F has bounded L^2 norm and z'=F'=(1/2)B_t(f,f), whose H^(-pstar) norm is bounded by N005, so ||z||_X<=C_(gamma,M0).

produces.statement: Under L1, ||f||_2<=M0+1, q<=2, sup_I||F||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0), sup_I||F-Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^1)<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta, sup_I(||F||_(H^(a_gamma))+||F||_2)<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, and ||z||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0).

argument.text: Set Astage=Fstage_(a,t)(w) and Dstage=F-Astage. Apply the product bound in N006 to partial_x(S_t Astage) and S_t Astage, using the H^(1+gamma) and H^(a_gamma) stage bounds. It gives ||partial_x[(S_t Astage)^2]||_2<=2*C_gamma||Astage||_(H^(1+gamma))||Astage||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau^gamma. The difference of squares is (S_t Dstage)*S_t(F+Astage). The H^1 algebra estimate in N005 and F001 give its derivative norm <=C_(gamma,M0)*delta. Therefore sup_I||B_t(F,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Integrating yields sup||Q||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q. N004 with exponent gamma and the current f,w then bounds Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f) by the same quantity, so ||W||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_I||B_t(F,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q and sup_I||Q||_2+||W||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

argument.text: Since Dinv B_t(f,F)=S_(-t)P[(S_t f)(S_t F)], split f=w+(f-w). N006 bounds the w product by C_gamma||w||_(H^gamma)||F||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q using F001. For the other product use ||f-w||_2||S_t F||_infinity<=C_(gamma,M0)*delta by the uniform H^1 stage bound and N005. Thus sup||Dinv B_t(f,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. Differentiating the definition Y=Cst+Q-((t-a)/tau)W gives Y'=B_t(f,F)+(1/2)B_t(F,F)-W/tau. N005, F002 and this asymmetric product estimate give sup||Dinv Y'||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. As Y(a)=0, integration gives sup||Dinv Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_I||Dinv B_t(f,F)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q, Y'=B_t(f,F)+(1/2)B_t(F,F)-W/tau, sup_I||Dinv Y'||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q and sup_I||Dinv Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

argument.text: Apply the normal form of N005 to Cst=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s))ds, with f constant, F(a)=0 and F'=(1/2)B(f,f). Symmetry and the J(B,h)-to-Ctri identity give exactly Cst(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F(t))-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](f,f,f). Its J term is O(q) in L^2 by N005 and F001. In its Ctri term use N006 with exponent gamma on (w,w,w) to get O(tau^gamma). Expand the difference from (f,f,f) into three trilinear differences and use N006 with exponent zero on each; their size is O(delta*(||f||_2+||w||_2)^2). Thus sup||Cst||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. With F002 in Y=Cst+Q-affine W this gives sup||Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

produces.statement: Under L1, Cst(t)=(1/3)J_t(f,F(t))-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](f,f,f), and sup_I||Y||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*q.

argument.text: All stage components are mean-zero because B and Rem have zero output mean. N005 gives ||Y'||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv Y'||_2 and ||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv Y||_2. Combine F003 and F004 to obtain ||Y||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q and sup||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q. These constants depend only on gamma and M0; none uses a higher norm of f.

produces.statement: Under L1, ||Y||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q and sup_I||Y||_(H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).

P=I-P0.

For 0<gamma<=1, M0>=1, a>=0,0<tau<=1 and smooth mean-zero real f,w with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 and ||f-w||_2<=1, put q=tau^gamma+||f-w||_2 and take the tuple (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y)=Interp_(a,tau;f); define rho(t)=-integral_a^t B_s(Y,z)ds-(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(Y,Y)ds-((t-a)/tau)*W on [a,a+tau]. Then Vst'=(1/2)B_t(Vst,Vst)+rho', rho'=-B_t(Y,z)-(1/2)B_t(Y,Y)-W/tau, sup||rho||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*tau*q, and ||rho'||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C_(gamma,M0)*q. On a smooth numerical trajectory and smooth exact twisted solution v with sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, concatenate these increments into Rres(0)=0, and let V be its continuous concatenation with grid values V(t_n)=v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. Then V'=(1/2)B_t(V,V)+Rres'. If I=[a,b] starts at a grid point, h=b-a<=1, e=v-V and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, including an endpoint inside a step, one has sup_(t in I)||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_(X(I))+||V||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0). The constants are independent of grid index, timestep, spectral support and higher norms.

binders.type: smooth exact twisted path satisfying v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v)

output.statement: Fix 0<gamma<=1 and M0>=1. There exist delta0 in (0,1] and K0>0, depending only on gamma,M0, with the following property. For any 0<tau<=delta0/2, any smooth real mean-zero exact twisted path v satisfying v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, and any smooth real mean-zero numerical trajectory with interpolation V obtained from Interp at its grid values, let e=v-V. On every interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, with h=b-a<=delta0 and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, one has E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma. The endpoint b may lie inside a step. More precisely the proof gives for all N>=2,h<=1,0<tau<=1 under this bootstrap: e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)), F_I(t)=integral_a^t B_s(e,v-e/2)ds; sup_I||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I; F_I=(1/3)[J_s(e,v-e/2)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,v-e/2,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds; sup_I||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I; and E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. Here Rres is the concatenation of the step increments rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,z_n)ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,Y_n)ds-((t-t_n)/tau)W_n, where the subscripted tuple is Interp_(t_n,tau;v^n), with Rres(0)=0, and every constant is independent of time index, timestep, spectral support and higher norms.

locals.declaration: Fix 0<tau<=1, with the smaller final restriction imposed later.
Fix the exact twisted path v.
Fix the interpolation V of the specified numerical trajectory.
Fix a grid starting point a.
Use the concatenated step residual defined by N009.
Fix an arbitrary proof-only threshold N>=2.
Let Hproj be the identity operator minus Lproj.
Choose C0>=1 dominating the finite constants in F005, uniformly over admissible intervals and trajectories.

argument.text: H002 supplies 0<gamma<=1. Assume L1: the smooth real mean-zero v satisfies v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, and the numerical interpolation V is taken on an interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, h<=1, E_I<=1. Set e=v-V,g=v-e/2 and take the concatenated Rres from N009. Its conclusions apply to this trajectory and give the accumulated residual and X bounds. In particular e'=B_t(e,g)-Rres', so integration gives e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)). Also ||e||_X<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||v||_X+||V||_X+||g||_X<=C_(gamma,M0).

produces.statement: Under L1, e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)), sup_I||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0)*(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_(X(I))+||V||_(X(I))+||g||_(X(I))<=C_(gamma,M0).

argument.text: Fix N>=2 only in the proof. For each time s, the inverse-product bound of N005 and the Fourier inequality ||Ple_N partial_x^2 A||_2<=N^2||A||_2 give ||Ple_N B_s(e,g)||_2<=C*N^2||e||_2||g||_2. Indeed B_s(e,g)=S_(-s)partial_x^2 Dinv P[(S_s e)(S_s g)]. Integrate over length at most h and use bounded ||g||_2 to obtain sup||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1, for every N>=2, sup_I||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I.

argument.text: Apply the two-endpoint normal form N005 to F_I. The equations give e'=B(e,g)-Rres' and g'=(1/2)B(v,v)-(1/2)B(e,g)+(1/2)Rres'. In the differentiated J terms, its symmetry and integral J(B,h)=Ctri give Ctri(e,g,g)-(1/2)Ctri(e,g,e)=Ctri(e,g,V), since g-e/2=V. The other cubic term is (1/2)Ctri(v,v,e), and the forcing terms satisfy -J(Rres',g)+(1/2)J(e,Rres')=-J(Rres',V). Multiplication by -1/3 yields F_I=(1/3)[J_s(e,g)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds. Both endpoints are retained. Apply the H^1 bound for J in N005: their projections above N are <=C_(gamma,M0)*N^(-1)*E_I. Continuity of all the paths makes internal endpoints cancel when the normal form is applied stepwise.

produces.statement: Under L1, F_I(t)=(1/3)[J_s(e,g)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds. The sum of the norms of Pgt_N J_t(e,g) and Pgt_N J_a(e,g) is <=C_(gamma,M0)*N^(-1)*E_I.

argument.text: For any three admissible paths on I, put Lproj=Ple_(N/3),Hproj equal to the identity operator minus Lproj. The telescoping expansion Ctri(f_1,f_2,f_3)-Ctri(Lproj f_1,Lproj f_2,Lproj f_3)=Ctri(Hproj f_1,f_2,f_3)+Ctri(Lproj f_1,Hproj f_2,f_3)+Ctri(Lproj f_1,Lproj f_2,Hproj f_3) places a high input in each term. The all-low term has no output above N because all product frequencies sum. Each projection contracts both components of X and ||Hproj f_i||_(H^(-pstar))<=C*N^(-pstar)||f_i||_2 by Fourier weights. Apply N006 with the negative norm on that particular high slot. This proves ||Pgt_N Ctri_I(f_1,f_2,f_3)||_2<=C*h*product_j||f_j||_X+C*N^(-pstar)*product_j||f_j||_(L^infinity L^2). Apply this to (e,g,V) and (v,v,e), using F001: their total contribution is <=C_(gamma,M0)*h*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I.

produces.statement: Under L1, ||Pgt_N Ctri_[a,t](e,g,V)||_2+||Pgt_N Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*h*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+N^(-pstar))*E_I uniformly for t in I.

argument.text: For the remaining integral in F003 substitute the actual stepwise Rres' formula from N009, and use integral J(B,h)=Ctri from N005 on each intersected step segment. It becomes -Ctri(Y_n,z_n,V)-(1/2)Ctri(Y_n,Y_n,V)-tau^(-1)integral J_s(W_n,V)ds. At that step's start, delta_n=||e(t_n)||_2<=E_I. N008 gives ||Y_n||_X<=C*q_n, ||Y_n||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))<=C*tau*q_n, ||z_n||_X<=C and ||W_n||_2<=C*tau*q_n. N006, with the negative norm on Y_n, bounds the first two terms by C*tau*q_n (using q_n<=2 and ||V||_X<=C from F001). The last term is also <=C*tau*q_n by the L^2 J bound from N005. These remain valid upper bounds on a partial final step. At most h/tau+1 steps are met, and q_n<=tau^gamma+E_I. Thus the forcing integral is bounded by C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I).

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_(t in I)||integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I). All constants in this bound and the endpoint, cubic, low-frequency and accumulated residual bounds can be dominated by a single positive constant depending only on gamma,M0, uniformly over admissible trajectories, intervals, timesteps and thresholds N>=2.

argument.text: Combine F003-F005 to obtain sup||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. With F002, the exact error identity and residual bound in F001 give E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. All constants are uniform in the parameters specified in F005.

produces.statement: Under L1, sup_I||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I, and E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I, with one constant depending only on gamma,M0.

argument.text: Choose C0>=1 dominating these constants from F005-F006, independently of all the particular paths. Define N0=ceil(max(2,16*C0,(16*C0)^(1/pstar))). Then C0*(N0^(-1)+N0^(-pstar))<=1/8<=1/4. Put delta0=min(1,1/(8*C0*(N0^2+3))) and K0=4*C0. If h<=delta0 and tau<=delta0/2, then C0*(N0^2*h+h+tau)<=C0*delta0*(N0^2+3)<=1/8<=1/4. F006 therefore has E_I coefficient at most 1/2. Absorption gives E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+2*C0*(h+tau)*tau^gamma<=2||e(a)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma. These choices depend only on gamma,M0. Discharge L1, retaining its antecedents in the conditional theorem, and quantify all trajectories, intervals and timesteps. This proves the output assertion.

definitions.definition: Torus=ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), with measure dx/(2*pi) on [0,2*pi). Here ℝ denotes the real number system, distinct from the radius parameter R.
For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).

definitions.type: homogeneous Sobolev norms on the mean-zero subspaces

definitions.definition: S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
P0 f=hat f(0), the mean, identified with a constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1); hat(Dinv f)(k)=(i*k)^(-1)hat f(k) for k!=0 and zero for k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). These formulas define maps H^s -> H^(s+1) and H^s -> H^(s+2), respectively.
For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L^2, Ftau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2].

H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
Notation in this copied formula: H_tau=Htau at timestep tau, F_tau=Ftau, P_0=P0, D^(-1)=Dinv and D^(-2)=(Dinv)^2=Dinv2; S_r is the group S at time r. The bracket variable G denotes the entire expression depending on s inside that bracket.

definitions.type: unmodified time-step map and finite numerical trajectories
definitions.definition: Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f), tau>0. For a positive integer Lsteps and tau=T/Lsteps>0, set t_n=n*tau and u^0=u_0, u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n), 0<=n<Lsteps; v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. No spatial frequency cutoff is applied. This is a finite recursion; its L^2 continuity and preservation properties are proved below.
Ple_N f has coefficients 1_(|k|<=N)*hat f(k), N>=0; Pgt_N=I-Ple_N. These are used only in the proof and in initial-data approximation.
Mavg_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds, tau>0.

definitions.type: average covariance of two exponential phases
definitions.definition:
For real alpha,beta,
M_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds,
eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
The notation M_tau here means Mavg_tau; eta_tau is the family eta at timestep tau.

definitions.type: smooth-input trilinear averaged cubic remainder with a polynomial dense core
definitions.definition: For tau>0,t0>=0 and mean-zero trigonometric polynomials f_1,f_2,f_3, define hat(Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3))(k)=-tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f_1(a)*hat f_2(b)*hat f_3(c) for k!=0, and zero at k=0. Here p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. The notation R^n_(2,tau) means Rem_(n*tau,tau). The extension to Sobolev inputs is a proved conclusion below, not an assumed estimate. The same Fourier formula defines the operator for smooth inputs by absolutely convergent series: |eta|<=2 from the two averages and smooth Fourier coefficients are rapidly decreasing, so the triple sum is absolutely convergent. The polynomial restriction is its initial dense core.
pstar=23/14.

For an interval I with length at most one, X(I) consists of L^infinity(I;L^2) functions with weak time derivative in L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar)); ||f||_(X(I))=||f||_(L^infinity(I;L^2))+||f'||_(L^infinity(I;H^(-pstar))). All time suprema of continuous functions use their continuous representatives; derivatives and L^infinity norms use essential suprema.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.
J_t(f,g)=S_(-t)P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

Ctri_I(f,g,h)=integral_I S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. For time-independent inputs suppress their t dependence. Initially use smooth spatial inputs, with piecewise smooth continuous time dependence; bounded extensions are justified by the explicit sources or estimates below.
Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/2) integral_a^t B_s(f,g) ds for time-independent smooth mean-zero f,g and a<=t. Fstage_(a,t)(f) abbreviates Fstage_(a,t)(f,f).

For a>=0,tau>0 and smooth mean-zero f, on [a,a+tau] put F(t)=Fstage_(a,t)(f), z(t)=f+F(t), Cst(t)=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s)) ds, Q(t)=(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(F(s),F(s)) ds, W=Q(a+tau)+Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f), Vst(t)=f+F(t)+Cst(t)+Q(t)-((t-a)/tau)*W, Y(t)=Vst(t)-z(t). Interp_(a,tau;f) denotes this entire tuple (F,z,Cst,Q,W,Vst,Y). It is just these formulas, with no error estimates or endpoint matching granted.

KdV(u;u_0) means u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u_0 on Torus, distributionally. The exact solution sought for real mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation. This predicate itself asserts no existence or quantitative bound.

inputs.statement: 0<gamma<=1.

There is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero datum a0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||a0||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique real mean-zero exact KdV solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma), obtained by smooth approximation, satisfying sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth data have smooth solutions. If a0,b0 are two such data then sup_[0,T]||u_a0(t)-u_b0(t)||_2<=K(T,2*R)||a0-b0||_2. The same estimate holds for any two real mean-zero L^2 data with sum of norms <=2*R. Twisting v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) preserves these bounds; for smooth data v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v). Thus M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma)<=1+A uniformly on the original ball.

For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau is a continuous map on the real mean-zero L^2 space, preserves mean zero and reality, and maps smooth data to smooth data; Ftau:L^2->H^1 is continuous. Hence all finite numerical trajectories are defined and continuous in the initial datum. For every smooth mean-zero real f, tau>0 and integer n>=0, S_(-(n+1)*tau)Psi_tau(S_(n*tau)f)=f+Fstage_(n*tau,(n+1)*tau)(f)+integral_(n*tau)^((n+1)*tau)B_s(f,Fstage_(n*tau,s)(f))ds-Rem_(n*tau,tau)(f,f,f). Consequently on a numerical smooth trajectory the tuple Interp_(t_n,tau;v^n) has Vst(t_n)=v^n and Vst(t_(n+1))=v^(n+1). The interpolants therefore concatenate to a continuous piecewise smooth mean-zero real V on [0,T].

Fix 0<gamma<=1 and M0>=1. There exist delta0 in (0,1] and K0>0, depending only on gamma,M0, with the following property. For any 0<tau<=delta0/2, any smooth real mean-zero exact twisted path v satisfying v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v), sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=M0, and any smooth real mean-zero numerical trajectory with interpolation V obtained from Interp at its grid values, let e=v-V. On every interval I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, with h=b-a<=delta0 and E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1, one has E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+K0*delta0*tau^gamma. The endpoint b may lie inside a step. More precisely the proof gives for all N>=2,h<=1,0<tau<=1 under this bootstrap: e(t)=e(a)+F_I(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)), F_I(t)=integral_a^t B_s(e,v-e/2)ds; sup_I||Ple_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*N^2*h*E_I; F_I=(1/3)[J_s(e,v-e/2)]_a^t-(1/3)Ctri_[a,t](e,v-e/2,V)-(1/6)Ctri_[a,t](v,v,e)+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds; sup_I||Pgt_N F_I||_2<=C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I; and E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_(gamma,M0)*(h+tau)*tau^gamma+C_(gamma,M0)*(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-pstar))*E_I. Here Rres is the concatenation of the step increments rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,z_n)ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,Y_n)ds-((t-t_n)/tau)W_n, where the subscripted tuple is Interp_(t_n,tau;v^n), with Rres(0)=0, and every constant is independent of time index, timestep, spectral support and higher norms.

output.statement: There exist Csm>0 and tausm>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every smooth real mean-zero initial datum u_0 with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer Lsteps with tau=T/Lsteps<=tausm, the exact solution u and unfiltered numerical trajectory satisfy sup_(0<=t<=T)||S_(-t)u(t)-V(t)||_2<=Csm*tau^gamma and max_(0<=n<=Lsteps)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=Csm*tau^gamma, where V is the interpolation of Interp at v^n=S_(-n*tau)u^n. All constants are uniform in the full stated smooth-data ball, Fourier support and higher norms.

locals.declaration: Choose a uniform flow bound A from F001.
Choose the common stability length delta0 from F002.
Choose K0 together with delta0 from F002.
Put tau=T/Lsteps under the positive-integer antecedent.
Take the unique exact flow for u_0 from N001 under L1.
Use the numerical interpolation from N007 with initial datum u_0.

argument.text: H001-H003 give T>0,0<gamma<=1,R>0. N001 supplies a finite uniform H^gamma bound A(T,gamma,R) for the exact flow over this entire ball; enlarging it to a nonnegative value is harmless. In particular, record F001: there exists such an A, simultaneously valid for all data in the ball, and smooth data have smooth exact flows.

produces.statement: There exists A>=0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero datum uinit in H^gamma with ||uinit||_(H^gamma)<=R, the unique smooth-approximation exact solution uflow of KdV(uflow;uinit) satisfies sup_(0<=t<=T)||uflow(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A. definitions.definition: Torus=ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), with measure dx/(2*pi) on [0,2*pi). Here ℝ denotes the real number system, distinct from the radius parameter R.
For a periodic integrable f and k in Z, Fourier(f)(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; write hat f(k). Extend by completion and distribution duality.

For real s, H^s(Torus) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials for ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z)(1+k^2)^s |hat f(k)|^2. Negative spaces are periodic distributions. L^2=H^0 with the normalized measure. Real means hat f(-k)=overline(hat f(k)); mean-zero means hat f(0)=0. Write ||.||_2 for ||.||_(L^2).

definitions.type: homogeneous Sobolev norms on the mean-zero subspaces

definitions.definition: S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k). Thus S_(t+r)=S_t S_r, S_0=I and each S_t is an isometry on every H^s by its unit-modulus multiplier.
P0 f=hat f(0), the mean, identified with a constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1); hat(Dinv f)(k)=(i*k)^(-1)hat f(k) for k!=0 and zero for k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). These formulas define maps H^s -> H^(s+1) and H^s -> H^(s+2), respectively.
For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L^2, Ftau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2].

H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
Notation in this copied formula: H_tau=Htau at timestep tau, F_tau=Ftau, P_0=P0, D^(-1)=Dinv and D^(-2)=(Dinv)^2=Dinv2; S_r is the group S at time r. The bracket variable G denotes the entire expression depending on s inside that bracket.

definitions.type: unmodified time-step map and finite numerical trajectories
definitions.definition: Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f), tau>0. For a positive integer Lsteps and tau=T/Lsteps>0, set t_n=n*tau and u^0=u_0, u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n), 0<=n<Lsteps; v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. No spatial frequency cutoff is applied. This is a finite recursion; its L^2 continuity and preservation properties are proved below.
Ple_N f has coefficients 1_(|k|<=N)*hat f(k), N>=0; Pgt_N=I-Ple_N. These are used only in the proof and in initial-data approximation.
Mavg_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds, tau>0.

definitions.type: average covariance of two exponential phases
definitions.definition:
For real alpha,beta,
M_tau g=(1/tau) integral_0^tau g(s) ds,
eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
The notation M_tau here means Mavg_tau; eta_tau is the family eta at timestep tau.

definitions.type: smooth-input trilinear averaged cubic remainder with a polynomial dense core
definitions.definition: For tau>0,t0>=0 and mean-zero trigonometric polynomials f_1,f_2,f_3, define hat(Rem_(t0,tau)(f_1,f_2,f_3))(k)=-tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f_1(a)*hat f_2(b)*hat f_3(c) for k!=0, and zero at k=0. Here p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. The notation R^n_(2,tau) means Rem_(n*tau,tau). The extension to Sobolev inputs is a proved conclusion below, not an assumed estimate. The same Fourier formula defines the operator for smooth inputs by absolutely convergent series: |eta|<=2 from the two averages and smooth Fourier coefficients are rapidly decreasing, so the triple sum is absolutely convergent. The polynomial restriction is its initial dense core.
pstar=23/14.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic inputs, and in H^(-pstar) for L^2 inputs by the bound proved below.
Fstage_(a,t)(f,g)=(1/2) integral_a^t B_s(f,g) ds for time-independent smooth mean-zero f,g and a<=t. Fstage_(a,t)(f) abbreviates Fstage_(a,t)(f,f).

For a>=0,tau>0 and smooth mean-zero f, on [a,a+tau] put F(t)=Fstage_(a,t)(f), z(t)=f+F(t), Cst(t)=integral_a^t B_s(f,F(s)) ds, Q(t)=(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(F(s),F(s)) ds, W=Q(a+tau)+Rem_(a,tau)(f,f,f), Vst(t)=f+F(t)+Cst(t)+Q(t)-((t-a)/tau)*W, Y(t)=Vst(t)-z(t). KdV(u;u_0) means u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u_0 on Torus, distributionally. The exact solution sought for real mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation. This predicate itself asserts no existence or quantitative bound.

inputs.statement: 0<gamma<=1.

There is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero datum a0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||a0||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique real mean-zero exact KdV solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma), obtained by smooth approximation, satisfying sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A. The same estimate holds for any two real mean-zero L^2 data with sum of norms <=2*R. Twisting v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) preserves these bounds; for smooth data v'=(1/2)B_t(v,v). Consequently on a numerical smooth trajectory the tuple Interp_(t_n,tau;v^n) has Vst(t_n)=v^n and Vst(t_(n+1))=v^(n+1). The interpolants therefore concatenate to a continuous piecewise smooth mean-zero real V on [0,T].

There exist Csm>0 and tausm>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every smooth real mean-zero initial datum u_0 with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer Lsteps with tau=T/Lsteps<=tausm, the exact solution u and unfiltered numerical trajectory satisfy sup_(0<=t<=T)||S_(-t)u(t)-V(t)||_2<=Csm*tau^gamma and max_(0<=n<=Lsteps)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=Csm*tau^gamma, where V is the interpolation of Interp at v^n=S_(-n*tau)u^n. All constants are uniform in the full stated smooth-data ball, Fourier support and higher norms.

output.statement: There exist C>0 and tau_0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma(Torus) with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer Lsteps with tau=T/Lsteps<=tau_0, the exact solution of KdV(u;u_0) exists with the stipulated smooth-approximation meaning and the unfiltered recursion u^0=u_0, u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n) satisfies max_(0<=n<=Lsteps)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. Both constants are uniform on the entire initial-data ball and independent of Fourier support and additional smoothness.

Since T>0, this tau is positive. N001 supplies its unique exact solution u with the stipulated smooth-approximation meaning. Define u0seq_m=Ple_m u_0. argument.text: For each m, F002 yields max_n||useq_m(n*tau)-unumseq_m^n||_2<=C*tau^gamma. Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with the standing definitions of Section 2 of the supplied paper.

Use normalized measure dx/(2*pi) on the torus \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/(2*pi \mathbb{Z}). The Fourier coefficient is
\hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx,
and ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2s)|\hat f(k)|^2, where <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2).
These spaces are the completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms; negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. The normalized L^2 norm is the s=0 norm. For mean-zero functions, the homogeneous norm uses |k|^(2s) in place of <k>^(2s). For s>=0,
||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s);
for s<0, 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=||f||_(dot H^s).
Real-valued means \hat f(-k)=overline(\hat f(k)), and mean-zero means \hat f(0)=0.
All time suprema concern continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

Let S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), so \widehat{S_t f}(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)\hat f(k).
Let P_0 be the mean and P=I-P_0. Let D^(-1)=partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k!=0 and zero at k=0; D^(-2)=(D^(-1))^2.

The exact solution u is the unique real, mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation and satisfies this equation distributionally.

u^(n+1)=S_tau u^n+F_tau(u^n)+H_tau(u^n), 0<=n<L, [Eq. (2)]
where
F_tau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(D^(-1)f)^2],
H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
This is the fixed scheme of the paper's reference [1, Eq. (1.4)], without a spatial frequency cutoff.

max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2)<=C*tau^gamma.
The same C and tau_0 apply to the entire stated initial-data ball; no spectral support bound or additional smoothness is a hypothesis.

In the source's standing notation v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) and M=1+sup_(0<=t<=T)||v(t)||_(H^gamma).
Constants C_M may vary from line to line and depend on gamma,T,M, but are uniform in n,tau and spectral support. Section 2.1 supplies M<=1+A(T,gamma,R) uniformly on the ball using the cited exact-flow results; it is not an extra hypothesis on u_0. The source uses the continuous estimates from [1, Proposition 3.4 and Lemma 7.2] and does not use the logarithmic convergence theorem as an input.

value.author: Anatoli V. Babin; Alexei A. Ilyin; Edriss S. Titi
value.title: On the regularization mechanism for the periodic Korteweg-de Vries equation
hypotheses: The torus has length 2*pi, the datum is real and mean-zero.
The horizon Q is positive and the nonnegative Sobolev regularity and initial norms are as stated.
value.context: Source Sections 3-4 specify the homogeneous normalized norms and the coefficient solution notion. Theorem 4.2 gives uniform Galerkin bounds, 4.3 the limiting solution for positive s, 5.1 uniqueness and continuity for s>1/2, 6.3 for 0<s<=1/2, 6.4 for s=0. Uniformity on norm-bounded sets is the quantitative content of the estimates in their proofs, not a new hypothesis.
value.source_statement: Imported exact-flow clauses of the cited theorem suite: Theorem 4.2: if v^(m)(0)=v0 in dot H^s0, s0>=0, ||v^(m)(0)||_(dot H^0)<=M0 and T>0, then ||v^(m)(t)||_(dot H^s0)<=M_s0 on [0,T], uniformly in m, where M_s0 depends only on M0,T,||v0||_(dot H^s0),s0. Theorem 4.3: for s0>0, v0 in dot H^s0,T>0,0<sigma<s0, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,T];H^sigma), 1<p<infinity, and weak-* in L^infinity dot H^s0 to a solution of (3.8) in Definition 3.1, bounded by M_s0, with dot H^0 norm equal to its initial norm a.e. Theorem 5.1: for s>1/2 that solution is unique, C([0,T];dot H^s), Lipschitz in initial data as in (5.18), and conserves dot H^0 for all t. Theorem 6.3: for 0<s<=1/2 it is unique, C([0,T];dot H^s), and Lipschitz as in (6.7). Theorem 6.4: for s=0 there is a unique C([0,T];dot H^0) solution depending Lipschitz continuously on its data. Section 3 identifies these coefficient solutions with the physical U_t=UU_x+U_xxx; the proofs construct them by Galerkin or smooth limits.
value.notation_map: The source physical field is called U here; source twisted coefficients are z_k=exp(i*k^3*t)*hat U(k). Its normalized homogeneous Sobolev norms agree with Hdot. The reflection/sign bridge to our KdV is proved in N001.
value.errata: No correction affecting the imported statements was found in the accessed primary text. This records the scope of inspection, not a claim that no erratum exists elsewhere.
value.version_check: 2026-10-31: PDF cover and arXiv version record identify v2 dated 23 Oct 2010, with 42 numbered pages. The listed theorem numbers and conventions were read in that version; arXiv history lists v1 and v2.
value.qualification: Explicit proved statements in the identified primary research text, separate from the target paper and from numerical experiments; none imports a convergence result for this target.
value.statement: For the real mean-zero periodic equation U_t=U*U_x+U_xxx on ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), use hat U(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral U(x)exp(-i*k*x)dx, ||U||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2s)|hat U(k)|^2, and z_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t)hat U(t)(k). For every s>0 and horizon Q>0, every initial datum U_0 in dot H^s has a distributional solution with z in C([0,Q];dot H^s), unique in the source solution class (z in L^infinity dot H^0 satisfying z_k(t)-z_k(0)=(i*k/2)integral_0^t sum_(k1+k2=k)exp(i*3*k*k1*k2*r)z_k1(r)z_k2(r)dr). Its dot H^0 norm is conserved, and the flow depends Lipschitz continuously on the initial data in dot H^s, uniformly on bounded dot H^s sets on [0,Q]. The Galerkin approximations (with the nonlinear inputs and output projected to |k|<=m and high coefficients frozen) have dot H^s bounds uniform in m, depending only on s,Q, the initial dot H^s norm and an upper bound for the initial dot H^0 norm. For 0<sigma<s they admit a subsequence converging strongly in L^q([0,Q];dot H^sigma), 1<q<infinity, and weak-* in L^infinity dot H^s to this solution; the same dot H^s bound holds for the limit. For s=0 there is a unique C([0,Q];dot H^0) solution, conserving that norm and depending Lipschitz continuously on its data. These flows agree on overlapping regularity classes and are obtained by smooth approximation.

targets.statement:
Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with the standing definitions of Section 2 of the supplied paper.

Use normalized measure dx/(2*pi) on the torus \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/(2*pi \mathbb{Z}). The Fourier coefficient is
\hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx,
and ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2s)|\hat f(k)|^2, where <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2).
These spaces are the completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms; negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. The normalized L^2 norm is the s=0 norm. For mean-zero functions, the homogeneous norm uses |k|^(2s) in place of <k>^(2s). For s>=0,
||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s);
for s<0, 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=||f||_(dot H^s).
Real-valued means \hat f(-k)=overline(\hat f(k)), and mean-zero means \hat f(0)=0.
All time suprema concern continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

Let S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), so \widehat{S_t f}(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)\hat f(k).
Let P_0 be the mean and P=I-P_0. Let D^(-1)=partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k!=0 and zero at k=0; D^(-2)=(D^(-1))^2.
The equation is
u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2),  u(0)=u_0. [Eq. (1)]
The exact solution u is the unique real, mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation and satisfies this equation distributionally.

For a positive integer L and tau=T/L, the fixed time-semidiscrete scheme is u^0=u_0 and
u^(n+1)=S_tau u^n+F_tau(u^n)+H_tau(u^n), 0<=n<L, [Eq. (2)]
where
F_tau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(D^(-1)f)^2],
H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
This is the fixed scheme of the paper's reference [1, Eq. (1.4)], without a spatial frequency cutoff.

For every T>0, every 0<gamma<=1 and every R>0, there exist C>0 and tau_0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real, mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma(\mathbb{T}) with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau_0, this exact fixed scheme satisfies
max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2)<=C*tau^gamma.
The same C and tau_0 apply to the entire stated initial-data ball; no spectral support bound or additional smoothness is a hypothesis.

In the source's standing notation v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) and M=1+sup_(0<=t<=T)||v(t)||_(H^gamma).
Constants C_M may vary from line to line and depend on gamma,T,M, but are uniform in n,tau and spectral support. Section 2.1 supplies M<=1+A(T,gamma,R) uniformly on the ball using the cited exact-flow results; it is not an extra hypothesis on u_0. The source uses the continuous estimates from [1, Proposition 3.4 and Lemma 7.2] and does not use the logarithmic convergence theorem as an input.

value.statement: For tau>0, n>=0 integer, t_n=n*tau and a smooth real mean-zero f, let uold=S_(t_n)f and unew=Psi_tau(uold), with the displayed unfiltered update. Then S_(-(t_n+tau))unew=f+Fstage_(t_n,t_n+tau)(f)+integral_(t_n)^(t_n+tau) B_s(f,Fstage_(t_n,s)(f)) ds-Rem_(t_n,tau)(f,f,f). original_context.full_target:
Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with the standing definitions of Section 2 of the supplied paper.

Use normalized measure dx/(2*pi) on the torus \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/(2*pi \mathbb{Z}). The Fourier coefficient is
\hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx,
and ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2s)|\hat f(k)|^2, where <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2).
These spaces are the completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms; negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. The normalized L^2 norm is the s=0 norm. For mean-zero functions, the homogeneous norm uses |k|^(2s) in place of <k>^(2s). For s>=0,
||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s);
for s<0, 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=||f||_(dot H^s).
Real-valued means \hat f(-k)=overline(\hat f(k)), and mean-zero means \hat f(0)=0.
All time suprema concern continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

Let S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), so \widehat{S_t f}(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)\hat f(k).
Let P_0 be the mean and P=I-P_0. Let D^(-1)=partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k!=0 and zero at k=0; D^(-2)=(D^(-1))^2.
The equation is
u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)partial_x(u^2),  u(0)=u_0. [Eq. (1)]
The exact solution u is the unique real, mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) solution obtained by smooth approximation and satisfies this equation distributionally.

For a positive integer L and tau=T/L, the fixed time-semidiscrete scheme is u^0=u_0 and
u^(n+1)=S_tau u^n+F_tau(u^n)+H_tau(u^n), 0<=n<L, [Eq. (2)]
where
F_tau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(D^(-1)f)^2],
H_tau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau D^(-1)f)D^(-1)F_tau(f)]
 +(tau/9)(S_tau D^(-1)f)P_0(f^2)
 -(1/54)[S_(tau-s)D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1)f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
 -(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s)D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau)D^(-2)F_tau(f))(S_s D^(-1)f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
Each bracket [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0).
This is the fixed scheme of the paper's reference [1, Eq. (1.4)], without a spatial frequency cutoff.

For every T>0, every 0<gamma<=1 and every R>0, there exist C>0 and tau_0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real, mean-zero u_0 in H^gamma(\mathbb{T}) with ||u_0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau_0, this exact fixed scheme satisfies
max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2)<=C*tau^gamma.
The same C and tau_0 apply to the entire stated initial-data ball; no spectral support bound or additional smoothness is a hypothesis.

In the source's standing notation v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) and M=1+sup_(0<=t<=T)||v(t)||_(H^gamma).
Constants C_M may vary from line to line and depend on gamma,T,M, but are uniform in n,tau and spectral support. Section 2.1 supplies M<=1+A(T,gamma,R) uniformly on the ball using the cited exact-flow results; it is not an extra hypothesis on u_0. The source uses the continuous estimates from [1, Proposition 3.4 and Lemma 7.2] and does not use the logarithmic convergence theorem as an input.

Both constants are uniform on the entire initial-data ball and independent of Fourier support and additional smoothness.
